title.zh: 卷三十八 列傳第二十八 柳元景
title.raw: 卷三十八 列傳第二十八 柳元景 Volume 38 Biographies 28: Liu Yanjing

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十八

translations.literal: Biographies 28
translations.idiomatic: Biography 28

sentences.zh: 柳元景

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjing
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing

sentences.zh: 元景少便弓馬，數隨父伐蠻，以勇稱。

translations.literal: Yuanjing from youth was skilled with bow and horse; he often followed his father on campaigns against the Man, and was known for courage.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Yuanjing was adept with bow and horse; he repeatedly accompanied his father on expeditions against the southern tribes and won renown for valor.

sentences.zh: 寡言語，有器質，荊州刺史謝晦聞其名，要之，未及往而晦敗。

translations.literal: He spoke little yet had natural capacity; Jingzhou Inspector Xie Hui heard his name and invited him, but before he could go, Hui was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Taciturn and endowed with presence, he was invited by Xie Hui, Inspector of Jing Province, after Hui heard of his reputation—but before Yuanjing could arrive, Hui had already been defeated.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史劉道產深愛其能，會荊州刺史江夏王義恭復召之，道產謂曰：「久規相屈。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Inspector Liu Daochan deeply admired his ability; when Jingzhou Inspector Prince Jiangxia Yigong summoned him again, Daochan said: "I have long planned to bend you to my service.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daochan, Inspector of Yong Province, greatly valued his talent; when Prince Jiangxia Yigong, now Inspector of Jing Province, summoned him once more, Daochan said to him: "I have long wished to keep you in my service.

sentences.zh: 今貴王有召，難輒相留，乖意以為罔罔。

translations.literal: Now the honored prince has summoned you; I can hardly detain you at once—against my wish I feel empty and lost."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the august prince has called for you, I cannot simply hold you back; it goes against my wishes, and I feel utterly at a loss."

sentences.zh: 」服闋，累遷義恭司徒太尉城局參軍。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, he was repeatedly promoted to Army Controller in the City Bureau on Yigong's staff as Grand Tutor and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period was over, he rose through several posts to Army Controller in the City Bureau on Prince Yigong's staff as Grand Tutor and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 文帝見又知之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen saw him, he again took note of him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen noticed him on sight and took him into favor once more.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉道產在雍州有惠化，遠蠻歸懷皆出，緣沔為村落，戶口殷盛。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Daochan was in Yongzhou he had benevolent influence; distant Man who submitted all came forth, and along the Han they formed villages—the population flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, while Liu Daochan governed Yong Province with benevolent rule, distant tribes who submitted to his sway came out of the hills; along the Han River they formed settlements, and the registered population grew abundant.

sentences.zh: 及道產死，群蠻大為寇暴。

translations.literal: When Daochan died, the Man tribes greatly raided and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: After Daochan's death, the tribal peoples rose in widespread raids and violence.

sentences.zh: 孝武西鎮襄陽，義恭薦元景，乃以為武威將軍、隨郡太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was stationed in the west at Xiangyang; Yigong recommended Yuanjing, and he was appointed General of Martial Prestige and Administrator of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xiaowu held the western command at Xiangyang, Yigong recommended Yuanjing, who was then appointed General of Martial Prestige and Administrator of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 及至，廣設方略，斬獲數百，郡境肅然。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he broadly laid plans; he beheaded and captured several hundred, and the commandery borders became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he devised far-reaching strategy, killed or captured several hundred enemies, and brought the commandery to quiet order.

sentences.zh: 隨王誕鎮襄陽，元景徙為後軍中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Dan of Sui was stationed at Xiangyang, Yuanjing was transferred to Middle Army Controller in the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Sui held Xiangyang, Yuanjing was reassigned as Middle Army Controller on the Rear Army staff.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷大舉北侵，使諸鎮各出軍。

translations.literal: When the court launched a major northern invasion, it ordered each garrison to send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the court undertook a great northern campaign, every regional command was ordered to mobilize.

sentences.zh: 二十七年八月，誕遣尹顯祖出貲谷，魯方平、薛安都、龐法起入盧氏，田義仁出魯陽，加元景建威將軍，總統軍帥。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-seventh year, Dan sent Yin Xianzu out from Zigui, Lu Fangping, Xue Anadu, and Pang Faqi into Lushi, and Tian Yiren out from Luyang; Yuanjing was added as General Who Establishes Might and given overall command of the army leaders.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year twenty-seven, Dan dispatched Yin Xianzu from Zigui, Lu Fangping, Xue Anadu, and Pang Faqi into Lushi, and Tian Yiren from Luyang; Yuanjing was promoted to General Who Establishes Might and placed in supreme command of the field commanders.

sentences.zh: 後軍外兵參軍龐季明，三秦冠族，求入長安，招懷關、陝，乃自貲谷入盧氏。

translations.literal: Rear Army External Troops Controller Pang Jiming, a leading clan of the Three Qins, sought to enter Chang'an and win over Guanzhong and Shaan, and so entered Lushi from Zigui.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jiming, External Troops Controller of the Rear Army—a foremost family of the Three Qins—aimed to reach Chang'an and rally Guanzhong and the Shaan region, and advanced from Zigui into Lushi.

sentences.zh: 盧氏人趙難納之。

translations.literal: Zhao Nan of Lushi received him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Nan, a local leader in Lushi, welcomed him in.

sentences.zh: 元景率軍系進，以前鋒深入，懸軍無繼，馳遣尹顯祖入盧氏，以為諸軍聲援。

translations.literal: Yuanjing led the army in continuous advance; because the vanguard had penetrated deep and the army was isolated without follow-up, he urgently sent Yin Xianzu into Lushi as a supporting force for the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing pressed forward in close pursuit; with the vanguard far ahead and no reserves behind, he hurried Yin Xianzu into Lushi to stiffen the rear and give the whole force a rallying point.

sentences.zh: 元景以軍食不足，難可曠日相持，乃束馬懸車，引軍上百丈崖，出溫谷以入盧氏。

translations.literal: Yuanjing, because provisions were insufficient and a prolonged standoff was difficult, had horses packed and wagons hoisted, and led the army up the Hundred-zhang Cliff, exiting Warm Valley to enter Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies were short and a drawn-out stalemate was impossible, so Yuanjing had horses slung and carts winched up the Hundred-zhang Cliff, led his men through Warm Valley, and broke into Lushi.

sentences.zh: 法起諸軍進次方伯堆，去弘農城五里。

translations.literal: Faqi's armies advanced and encamped at Fangbo Mound, five li from Hongnong city.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Faqi's columns halted at Fangbo Mound, five li from the walls of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 元景引軍度熊耳山，安都頓軍弘農。

translations.literal: Yuanjing led the army across Bear's Ear Mountain; Anadu encamped at Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing crossed Bear's Ear Mountain while Anadu held Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 法起進據潼關，季明率方平、趙難諸軍向陝。

translations.literal: Faqi advanced and seized Tong Pass; Jiming led the armies of Fangping and Zhao Nan toward Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Faqi pushed forward and occupied Tong Pass; Jiming marched Fangping, Zhao Nan, and the rest toward Shan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，元景率眾至弘農，營于開方口。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yuanjing led the host to Hongnong and encamped at Kaifang Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yuanjing brought his main force to Hongnong and pitched camp at Kaifang Ford.

sentences.zh: 仍以元景為弘農太守。

translations.literal: Yuanjing was again appointed Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was concurrently named Administrator of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 初，安都留住弘農而諸軍已進陝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Anadu had remained at Hongnong while the other armies had already advanced on Shan.
translations.idiomatic: At first Anadu had stayed behind at Hongnong while the other columns were already pressing toward Shan.

sentences.zh: 元景既到，謂安都曰：「卿無坐守空城，而令龐公孤軍深入，宜急進軍。

translations.literal: When Yuanjing arrived, he said to Anadu: "You should not sit guarding an empty city while letting Lord Pang's isolated army penetrate deep—you ought to advance quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuanjing arrived, he told Anadu: "Do not sit idle in an empty town while Pang's lone detachment pushes deep into enemy country—march at once."

sentences.zh: 」眾軍並造陝下，列營以逼之，並大造攻具。

translations.literal: All armies together advanced below Shan, set camp in array to press it, and on a large scale built siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: All columns converged beneath Shan, ringed the city with camps, and set to building siege equipment on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 魏城臨河為固，恃險自守。

translations.literal: The Wei city faced the river as its rampart and relied on the terrain to defend itself.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei-held city hugged the river for protection and trusted the terrain to keep the attackers at bay.

sentences.zh: 季明、安都、方平、顯祖、趙難諸軍頻三攻未拔，安都、方平各列陣于城東南以待之。

translations.literal: The armies of Jiming, Anadu, Fangping, Xianzu, and Zhao Nan attacked three times in succession without taking it; Anadu and Fangping each drew up battle lines southeast of the city to await the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming, Anadu, Fangping, Xianzu, and Zhao Nan assaulted the place three times without success; Anadu and Fangping then formed ranks southeast of the walls to receive the Wei counterstroke.

sentences.zh: 魏兵大合，輕騎挑戰，安都瞋目橫矛，單騎突陣，四向奮擊，左右皆辟易，殺傷不可勝數，於是眾軍並鼓噪俱前。

translations.literal: Wei troops massed in great numbers; light cavalry offered challenge. Anadu glared and levelled his spear, charging the formation alone on horseback, striking fiercely in all directions; those to left and right all gave way, and the killed and wounded were beyond counting—whereupon all armies together shouted and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei host gathered in force, and their light horse rode out to provoke a fight. Anadu glared, couched his spear, and plunged alone into the enemy ranks, hacking on every side until men fell back from him in waves; the dead and wounded were beyond count, and at that the whole allied army roared forward as one.

sentences.zh: 魏多縱突騎，眾軍患之。

translations.literal: The Wei frequently sent out shock cavalry, and the allied armies were troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei kept loosing their shock cavalry, and the allied troops found it hard to endure.

sentences.zh: 安都怒甚，乃脫兜鍪，解所帶鎧，唯著絳衲兩當衫，馬亦去具裝，馳入賊陣。

translations.literal: Anadu was extremely angry; he removed his helmet, took off the armor he wore, and wore only a crimson quilted double-breasted jacket; his horse too was stripped of barding, and he galloped into the enemy formation.
translations.idiomatic: Furious beyond bearing, Anadu tore off helmet and mail, kept only a crimson quilted fighting jacket, stripped his horse of armor as well, and charged straight into the enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 猛氣咆勃，所向無前，當其鋒者無不應刃而倒。

translations.literal: His fierce spirit roared; wherever he went none could stand before him—those who met his point all fell at the stroke of the blade.
translations.idiomatic: His battle fury blazed; nothing stood in his path, and every man who met his spear went down as if cut at a touch.

sentences.zh: 如是者數四。

translations.literal: He did this four times.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated this charge four times over.

sentences.zh: 每入，眾無不披靡。

translations.literal: Each time he entered, the enemy ranks invariably broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Every time he plunged in, the enemy lines shattered before him.

sentences.zh: 魏軍之將至也，方平遣驛騎告元景。

translations.literal: When the Wei army was about to arrive, Fangping sent a courier to inform Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: As the Wei host was closing in, Fangping dispatched a fast rider to warn Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍糧盡，各餘數日食。

translations.literal: At that time the armies' grain was exhausted; each had only a few days' food left.
translations.idiomatic: By then every column was out of grain, with only a few days' rations remaining.

sentences.zh: 元景方督義租並上驢馬以為糧運之計，遣軍副柳元怙簡步騎二千以赴陝急，卷甲兼行，一宿而至。

translations.literal: Yuanjing was just then supervising righteous levies and sending up donkeys and horses for grain transport; he sent Army Deputy Liu Yuanhu to select two thousand foot and horse to hurry to Shan, marching in armor without pause—they arrived in one night.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was organizing local grain levies and requisitioning pack animals when he sent his deputy Liu Yuanhu with two thousand picked infantry and cavalry to Shan in emergency relief; they marched under arms without rest and reached the field in a single night.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，魏軍又出，列陣於城外。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day the Wei army came out again and drew up in formation outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: At first light the Wei came out once more and formed their battle lines beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 方平諸軍並成列，安都並領馬軍，方平悉勒步卒左右掎角之，余諸義軍方於城西南列陣。

translations.literal: Fangping's armies all completed their lines; Anadu jointly led the cavalry; Fangping fully deployed infantry on left and right as pincers, while the remaining allied armies were just then drawing up southwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping's troops finished forming up; Anadu took command of the horse; Fangping arrayed his foot soldiers on both flanks in support, while the other allied units were still deploying southwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 方平謂安都曰：「今勍敵在前，堅城在後，是吾取死之日。

translations.literal: Fangping said to Anadu: "Now with fierce enemies before us and a strong city behind, this is the day we must seek death."
translations.idiomatic: Fangping told Anadu: "With a formidable foe in front and a walled city at our backs, today is the day we stake our lives."

sentences.zh: 卿若不進，我當斬卿，我若不進，卿當斬我也。

translations.literal: If you do not advance, I shall behead you; if I do not advance, you shall behead me."
translations.idiomatic: If you fail to charge, I will cut off your head; if I fail to charge, you will cut off mine."

sentences.zh: 」安都曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: Anadu said: "What you say is right."
translations.idiomatic: Anadu replied: "You speak the truth."

sentences.zh: 」遂合戰。

translations.literal: They then joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: With that they closed and fought.

sentences.zh: 安都不堪其憤，橫矛直前，殺傷者甚多。

translations.literal: Anadu, unable to contain his rage, levelled his spear and charged straight ahead, killing and wounding a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to hold his fury in check, Anadu levelled his spear and drove straight in, killing and wounding a great many.

sentences.zh: 流血凝肘。

translations.literal: Blood congealed on his elbows.
translations.idiomatic: Blood clotted thick on his forearms.

sentences.zh: 矛折，易之復入，軍副譚金率騎從而奔之。

translations.literal: His spear broke; he replaced it and charged in again; Army Deputy Tan Jin led cavalry following in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When his spear snapped he seized another and plunged back in; Army Deputy Tan Jin swept after him with the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 自詰旦戰至日晏，魏軍大潰，面縛軍門者二千餘人。

translations.literal: From dawn until evening they fought; the Wei army was utterly routed, and more than two thousand came bound at the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: The battle ran from dawn to dusk; the Wei army broke in complete rout, and more than two thousand men came to the gate with hands bound.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲盡殺之，元景以為不可，乃悉釋而遣之。

translations.literal: The generals wished to kill them all; Yuanjing held that this could not be done, and released and sent them all away.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders wanted to slaughter them all, but Yuanjing forbade it and set every man free.

sentences.zh: 皆稱萬歲而去。

translations.literal: They all shouted "Long life!" and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They shouted their thanks and went their way.

sentences.zh: 時北略諸軍王玄謨等敗退，魏軍深入。

translations.literal: At that time the northern expedition armies under Wang Xuamo and others were defeated and withdrew; Wei troops penetrated deep.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Xuamo's northern expedition had been beaten back, and Wei forces were driving deep into Song territory.

sentences.zh: 文帝以元景不宜獨進，且令班師。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen considered that Yuanjing ought not advance alone, and moreover ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen judged that Yuanjing should not press forward alone and ordered a general withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 諸軍乃自湖關度白楊嶺出於長洲，安都斷後，宗越副之。

translations.literal: The armies then crossed from Huguan over White Poplar Ridge and emerged at Changzhou; Anadu covered the rear, with Zong Yue as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The columns withdrew through Huguan, crossed White Poplar Ridge, and came out at Changzhou; Anadu held the rear, assisted by Zong Yue.

sentences.zh: 法起自潼關向商城，與元景會，季明亦從胡谷南歸，並有功而入。

translations.literal: Faqi went from Tong Pass toward Shangcheng and joined Yuanjing; Jiming also returned south through Hugu Valley—all entered with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Faqi marched from Tong Pass toward Shangcheng and linked up with Yuanjing; Jiming came south through Hugu Valley as well, and all returned credited with achievement.

sentences.zh: 誕登城望之，以鞍下馬迎元景。

translations.literal: Dan mounted the wall to watch them; he dismounted from the saddle to welcome Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Dan climbed the city wall to watch them approach, then swung down from his saddle to greet Yuanjing in person.

sentences.zh: 時魯爽向虎牢，復使元景率安都等北出，爽退乃還。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Shuang moved on Hulao; Yuanjing was again sent north leading Anadu and others; when Shuang withdrew, they returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Shuang threatened Hulao, Yuanjing was once more sent north with Anadu and the rest; they came back after Shuang retreated.

sentences.zh: 再出北侵，威信著於境外。

translations.literal: Going out twice on northern campaigns, his prestige and trust were established beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: After two northern campaigns his authority was firmly established among the border peoples.

sentences.zh: 臧質、義宣並反，王玄謨南據梁山，垣護之、薛安都度據曆陽，元景出屯採石。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi and Yixuan both rebelled; Wang Xuamo held Liang Mountain in the south; Yuan Huzhi and Xue Anadu crossed and held Liyang; Yuanjing went out and encamped at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi and Liu Yixuan rose in revolt, Wang Xuamo seized Liang Mountain in the south, Yuan Huzhi and Xue Anadu crossed the Yangtze and held Liyang, and Yuanjing took post at Caishi.

sentences.zh: 玄謨求益兵，上使元景進屯姑孰。

translations.literal: Xuamo requested reinforcements; the emperor had Yuanjing advance and encamp at Gudu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuamo asked for more troops, and the emperor ordered Yuanjing forward to Gudu.

sentences.zh: 元景悉遣精兵助王玄謨，以羸弱居守。

translations.literal: Yuanjing sent all his elite troops to aid Wang Xuamo, keeping only the weak to hold the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing sent every picked soldier to Wang Xuamo's aid and kept only the feeblest men to hold his own position.

sentences.zh: 所遣軍多張旗幟，梁山望之如數萬人，皆謂都下兵悉至，由是克捷。

translations.literal: The troops he sent displayed many banners and flags; from Liang Mountain they looked like tens of thousands—all thought the capital's armies had fully arrived, and thereby victory was won.
translations.idiomatic: His detachments flew a forest of banners; from Liang Mountain they looked like tens of thousands of men, and the rebels believed the full capital army had arrived—victory followed from that deception.

sentences.zh: 與沈慶之俱以本號加開府儀同三司，改封晉安郡公。

translations.literal: He and Shen Qingzhi were both given their existing titles plus Grand Master with Golden Seal and Banners Equal to the Three Dukes, and his fief was changed to Duke of Jin'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shen Qingzhi were both promoted in their existing ranks to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Banners Equal to the Three Dukes, and Yuanjing's title was changed to Duke of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 固讓開府。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the establishment of a separate office.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the separate grand office.

sentences.zh: 復為領軍、太子詹事，加侍中。

translations.literal: He was again made Director of the Imperial Guards and Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the added title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed Director of the Imperial Guards and Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the added rank of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，為尚書令，太子詹事、侍中、中正如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Palace Attendant, and Chief Commandant remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Daming era he was made Director of the Imperial Secretariat, retaining his posts as Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Palace Attendant, and Chief Commandant.

sentences.zh: 以封在嶺南，改封巴東郡公。

translations.literal: Because his fief was beyond the southern ranges, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Badong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because his original fief lay south of the ranges, his title was changed to Duke of Badong.

sentences.zh: 又命左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，侍中、令、中正如故。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Banners Equal to the Three Dukes; Palace Attendant, Director, and Chief Commandant remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further named Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Banners Equal to the Three Dukes, while retaining Palace Attendant, Secretariat Director, and Chief Commandant.

sentences.zh: 又讓開府。

translations.literal: He again declined the separate grand office.
translations.idiomatic: Once again he declined the separate grand office.

sentences.zh: 乃與沈慶之俱依晉密陵侯鄭袤不受司空故事。

translations.literal: He and Shen Qingzhi both followed the Jin precedent of Marquis Milin Zheng Mao, who had refused the post of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shen Qingzhi both invoked the Jin precedent of Zheng Mao, Marquis of Milin, who had refused the office of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 六年，進司空，侍中、令、中正如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was advanced to Minister of Works; Palace Attendant, Director, and Chief Commandant remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Minister of Works, retaining Palace Attendant, Secretariat Director, and Chief Commandant.

sentences.zh: 又固讓。

translations.literal: He again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He declined once more.

sentences.zh: 乃授侍中、驃騎大將軍、南兗州刺史，留衛都下。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, remaining to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Southern Yan Province, with orders to remain and guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝武晏駕，與太宰江夏王義恭、尚書僕射顏師伯並受遺詔輔幼主，遷尚書令，領丹陽尹，侍中、將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, he together with Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia Yigong and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yan Shibo all received the testamentary edict to assist the young lord; he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat, concurrently Administrator of Danyang, with Palace Attendant and General as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu's death, Yuanjing joined Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia Yigong and Vice Director Yan Shibo as regents under the late emperor's will; he was moved to Director of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrent Administrator of Danyang, retaining Palace Attendant and his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 加開府儀同三司，給班劍二十人。

translations.literal: He was given the added title Grand Master with Golden Seal and Banners Equal to the Three Dukes, with twenty halberd-bearing guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted Grand Master with Golden Seal and Banners Equal to the Three Dukes, with a guard of twenty ceremonial halberds.

sentences.zh: 固辭班劍。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the halberd guard.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 元景少時貧苦，嘗下都至大雷，日暮寒甚，頗有羇旅之歎。

translations.literal: When Yuanjing was young he was poor and hard pressed; once going down to the capital he reached Dalei, and at evening the cold was severe—he had many sighs of a traveler far from home.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yuanjing was poor; once, traveling toward the capital, he reached Dalei at nightfall in bitter cold and felt the full weight of a wanderer's loneliness.

sentences.zh: 岸側有一老父自稱善相，謂元景曰：「君方大富貴，位至三公。

translations.literal: On the bank an old man who called himself skilled in physiognomy said to Yuanjing: "Sir, you are about to attain great wealth and honor, rising to the rank of one of the Three Dukes."
translations.idiomatic: An old man on the shore who claimed skill in reading faces told him: "You are destined for great wealth and rank—one of the Three Dukes awaits you."

sentences.zh: 」元景以為戲之，曰：「人生免饑寒幸甚，豈望富貴。

translations.literal: Yuanjing took it as jest and said: "In life merely to escape hunger and cold is already fortunate—how could one hope for wealth and honor?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing took this for banter and replied: "Merely to escape hunger and cold is fortune enough—who dares dream of wealth and high office?"

sentences.zh: 」老父曰：「後當相憶。

translations.literal: The old man said: "Later you will remember this."
translations.idiomatic: The old man said: "You will remember this day."

sentences.zh: 」及貴求之，不知所在。

translations.literal: When he became eminent he sought him, but did not know where he was.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to power he searched for the man, but no one knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 元景起自將率，及當朝，理務雖非所長，而有弘雅之美。

translations.literal: Yuanjing rose from the ranks of generals; when he held court office, though administration was not his strength, he had the beauty of magnanimity and refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing had risen from the military ranks; in high office he was no master of routine administration, yet he carried himself with generous and cultivated grace.

sentences.zh: 時在朝勳要多事產業，惟元景獨無所營。

translations.literal: At that time meritorious ministers at court mostly pursued estates and enterprises; only Yuanjing undertook nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Most court nobles of the day busied themselves with estates and ventures; Yuanjing alone built nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 南岸有數十畝菜園，守園人賣菜得錢三萬，送還宅。

translations.literal: On the south bank he had several tens of mu of vegetable garden; the gardener sold vegetables and obtained thirty thousand cash, which he sent back to the residence.
translations.idiomatic: On the south bank he kept a vegetable plot of several dozen mu; the gardener sold produce for thirty thousand cash and brought the money to the house.

sentences.zh: 元景怒曰：「我立此園種菜，以供家中啖耳，乃復賣以取錢，奪百姓之利邪。

translations.literal: Yuanjing angrily said: "I established this garden to grow vegetables merely to supply the household's eating—yet you again sell for money and seize the people's profit?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing grew angry: "I planted this garden only to feed my household—how dare you sell the crop for cash and steal profit from the common people?"

sentences.zh: 」以錢乞守園人。

translations.literal: He gave the money to the gardener.
translations.idiomatic: He handed the money back to the gardener.

sentences.zh: 孝武嚴暴無常，元景雖荷寵遇，恒慮及禍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was stern, violent, and unpredictable; though Yuanjing enjoyed favor, he constantly feared disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was harsh, cruel, and erratic; though favored, Yuanjing lived in constant fear of ruin.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭及諸大臣莫不重足屏氣，未嘗敢私相往來。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia Yigong and all the great ministers none failed to tread as if on thin ice and hold their breath—they never dared privately visit one another.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia Yigong and every senior minister walked as if on eggshells and scarcely dared breathe; none ventured private visits to one another.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，義恭、元景等並相謂曰：「今日始免橫死。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu died, Yigong, Yuanjing, and the others all said to one another: "From today we are at last spared violent death."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu died, Yigong, Yuanjing, and the rest said to one another: "At last we are free of the fear of a sudden execution."

sentences.zh: 」義恭與義陽等諸王，元景與顏師伯等常相馳逐聲樂酣飲，以夜繼晝。

translations.literal: Yigong with the princes of Yiyang and others, and Yuanjing with Yan Shibo and others, often raced about together in music and deep drinking, continuing day from night.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong and the princes, Yuanjing and Yan Shibo and their circle, gave themselves over to racing, music, and heavy drinking, carrying their revels from night into day.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝少有凶德，內不能平，殺戴法興後，悖情轉露，義恭、元景憂懼，乃與師伯等謀廢帝立義恭，持疑未決。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor from youth had a vicious nature and could not find inner peace; after killing Dai Faxing his rebellious disposition increasingly showed. Yigong and Yuanjing were anxious and afraid, and with Shibo and others plotted to depose the emperor and establish Yigong—yet they hesitated and did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor's successor had been vicious from boyhood and could not govern himself; after he killed Dai Faxing his savagery showed plainly. Yigong and Yuanjing, in alarm, plotted with Shibo and others to remove the emperor and set Yigong on the throne, but they wavered and never acted.

sentences.zh: 發覺，帝親率宿衛兵自出討之，稱詔召元景。

translations.literal: When this was discovered, the emperor personally led the palace guard out to attack them, and in the emperor's name summoned Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was uncovered; the emperor led the palace guard in person and, under imperial summons, called Yuanjing to court.

sentences.zh: 左右奔告，兵刃非常。

translations.literal: Attendants ran to inform him; weapons were in extraordinary array.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants rushed in with word that armed men were massing in ominous array.

sentences.zh: 元景知禍至，整朝服乘車，應召出門。

translations.literal: Yuanjing knew disaster had come; he straightened his court robes, entered his carriage, and answered the summons by going out the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his end had come, Yuanjing straightened his court dress, entered his carriage, and went out to answer the summons.

sentences.zh: 逢弟車騎司馬叔仁戎服，左右壯士數十人，欲拒命。

translations.literal: He met his younger brother, Commandant of Cavalry Attendants Shuren, in military dress, with several tens of stalwart men at his side, wishing to resist the order.
translations.idiomatic: He met his brother Shuren, Commandant of Cavalry Attendants, in armor with several dozen strong men at his side, ready to resist by force.

sentences.zh: 元景苦禁之。

translations.literal: Yuanjing sternly forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing forbade them with all his authority.

sentences.zh: 及出巷，軍士大至，下車受戮，容色恬然。

translations.literal: When he left the lane, soldiers arrived in force; he descended from the carriage to receive execution, his expression calm.
translations.idiomatic: As he left the lane the troops closed in; he stepped down from his carriage to meet the blade, his face serene.

sentences.zh: 長子慶宗有幹力，而情性不倫，孝武使元景送還襄陽，於道賜死。

translations.literal: His eldest son Qingzong had ability and strength, but his disposition was unorthodox; Emperor Xiaowu had Yuanjing escort him back to Xiangyang, and on the road he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Qingzong was capable but wayward in character; Emperor Xiaowu had Yuanjing escort him back to Xiangyang, and he was ordered to take his own life on the road.

sentences.zh: 次子嗣宗、紹宗、茂宗、孝宗、文宗、仲宗、成宗、秀宗至是並遇禍。

translations.literal: His second sons Sizong, Shaozong, Maozong, Xiaozong, Wenzong, Zhongzong, Chengzong, and Xiuzong all met disaster on this occasion.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Sizong, Shaozong, Maozong, Xiaozong, Wenzong, Zhongzong, Chengzong, and Xiuzong all perished in the same purge.

sentences.zh: 元景六弟：僧景、僧珍、叔宗、叔政、叔珍、叔仁。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's six younger brothers were Sengjing, Sengzhen, Shuzong, Shuzheng, Shuzhen, and Shuren.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing had six younger brothers: Sengjing, Sengzhen, Shuzong, Shuzheng, Shuzhen, and Shuren.

sentences.zh: 僧珍、叔仁及子侄在都下襄陽死者數十人。

translations.literal: Sengzhen, Shuren, and sons and nephews at the capital and in Xiangyang who died numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen, Shuren, and dozens of sons and nephews at the capital and in Xiangyang died in the slaughter.

sentences.zh: 元景少子承宗、嗣宗子慕並在孕獲全。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's youngest son Chengzong and Sizong's son Mu, all still in the womb, were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing's youngest son Chengzong and Sizong's unborn son Mu were among the few who survived.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，贈太尉，給班劍三十人，羽葆、鼓吹一部，諡曰忠烈公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he was posthumously made Grand Commandant, given thirty halberd-bearing guards, a feather canopy and one set of martial music, and honored with the posthumous title Loyal and Fierce Duke.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming's accession, Yuanjing was posthumously named Grand Commandant, granted thirty ceremonial guards and a full martial escort, and given the posthumous title Duke of Loyal Valor.

sentences.zh: 元景從父兄元怙，大明末同晉安王子勳逆，事敗歸降。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's paternal cousin Yuanhu, at the end of Daming joined Prince Jin'an Zixun in rebellion, and when the affair failed returned in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing's cousin Yuanhu had joined Prince Jin'an Zixun's revolt in the last years of Daming and surrendered after its collapse.

sentences.zh: 元景從祖弟光世留鄉里，仕魏為河北太守，封西陵男，與司徒崔浩親。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's second cousin Guangshi remained in the homeland, served Wei as Administrator of Hebei, was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiling, and was intimate with Minister of Works Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: A more distant kinsman, Guangshi, had stayed in the north, served the Wei as Administrator of Hebei, held the title Baron of Xiling, and was close to Minister of Works Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩被誅，光世南奔。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed, Guangshi fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was put to death, Guangshi fled south to Song territory.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，位右衛將軍、順陽太守。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time he held the posts of General of the Right Guard and Administrator of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he served as General of the Right Guard and Administrator of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 子欣慰謀反，光世賜死。

translations.literal: His son Xinwei plotted rebellion; Guangshi was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Xinwei rebelled, Guangshi was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 世隆字彥緒，元景弟子也。

translations.literal: Shilong, style name Yanxu, was Yuanjing's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong, styled Yanxu, was Yuanjing's nephew.

sentences.zh: 父叔宗字雙驎，位建威參軍事，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Shuzong, style name Shuanglin, held the post of Army Controller on the staff of the General Who Establishes Might, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuzong, styled Shuanglin, had been an army controller on a general's staff and died young.

sentences.zh: 世隆幼孤，挺然自立，不與眾同。

translations.literal: Shilong was orphaned young; he stood upright and self-reliant, not going along with the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, Shilong held himself apart and refused to follow the crowd.

sentences.zh: 雖門勢子弟，獨修布衣之業。

translations.literal: Though a son of a powerful clan, he alone pursued the pursuits of a common scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Though born into a great house, he alone cultivated the life of a plain scholar.

sentences.zh: 及長，好讀書，折節彈琴，涉獵文史，音吐溫潤。

translations.literal: When grown, he loved reading, humbled himself to play the zither, ranged through literature and history, and his speech was warm and smooth.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he took to books, mastered the zither, ranged widely in letters and history, and spoke in a voice warm and measured.

sentences.zh: 元景愛賞，異于諸子，言于宋孝武，得召見。

translations.literal: Yuanjing loved and prized him, treating him differently from other sons, and spoke of him to Emperor Xiaowu of Song, so that he was summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing favored him above the other young men of the clan and commended him to Emperor Xiaowu, who summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 帝謂元景曰：「此兒將來復是三公一人。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yuanjing: "This boy in the future will again be one of the Three Dukes."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yuanjing: "This boy will one day rank among the Three Dukes."

sentences.zh: 」為西陽王撫軍法曹行參軍，出為武威將軍、上庸太守。

translations.literal: He was made Acting Army Controller in the Law Bureau on Prince Xiyang's Pacifying Army staff, then went out as General of Martial Prestige and Administrator of Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting legal officer on Prince Xiyang's staff, then sent out as General of Martial Prestige and Administrator of Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 帝謂元景曰：「卿昔以武威之號為隨郡，今復以授世隆，使卿門世不乏公也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yuanjing: "You once bore the title Martial Prestige in Suizhou; now I again grant it to Shilong, so that your house generation after generation will not lack a duke."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Yuanjing: "You once held the title General of Martial Prestige in Suizhou; I now give that same rank to Shilong, so your line may never lack a man of ducal standing."

sentences.zh: 元景為前廢帝所殺，世隆以在遠得免。

translations.literal: When Yuanjing was killed by the Former Deposed Emperor, Shilong because he was far away was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor's successor had Yuanjing executed, Shilong escaped because he was posted far away.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，四方反叛，世隆於上庸起兵以應宋明帝，為孔道存所敗，眾散逃隱，道存購之甚急。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, when the four quarters rebelled, Shilong raised troops at Shangyong to support Emperor Ming of Song; he was defeated by Kong Daocun, his forces scattered and hid, and Daocun offered a rich reward for his capture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taishi era, when rebellion flared on every side, Shilong raised forces at Shangyong for Emperor Ming but was beaten by Kong Daocun; his men scattered into hiding while Daocun offered a heavy price for his head.

sentences.zh: 軍人有貌相似者，斬送之。

translations.literal: A soldier with a similar appearance was beheaded and the head sent in.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier who resembled him was killed and his head sent in instead.

sentences.zh: 時世隆母郭妻閻並見縶襄陽獄，道存以所送首示之。

translations.literal: At that time Shilong's mother Guo and wife Yan were both imprisoned in Xiangyang jail; Daocun showed them the head that had been sent.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's mother Guo and his wife Yan were held in the Xiangyang prison; Daocun showed them the head.

sentences.zh: 母見首悲情小歇，而妻閻號叫方甚，竊謂郭曰：「今見不悲，為人所覺，唯當大慟以滅之。

translations.literal: When the mother saw the head her grief briefly eased, but wife Yan was wailing loudly; she whispered to Guo: "If we are not grief-stricken now, people will notice— we must wail greatly to conceal it."
translations.idiomatic: The mother, on seeing the head, checked her grief too soon, while Yan wailed loudly; Yan whispered to Guo: "If we do not mourn now, they will suspect us—we must cry out as if our hearts were broken."

sentences.zh: 」世隆竟以免。

translations.literal: Shilong in the end escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong himself ultimately escaped capture.

sentences.zh: 後為太子洗馬，與張緒、王延之、沈琰為君子之交。

translations.literal: Later he was made Palace Groom for the Heir Apparent, and with Zhang Xu, Wang Yanzhi, and Shen Yan formed friendships of true gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Palace Groom to the Heir Apparent and formed a circle of close friends with Zhang Xu, Wang Yanzhi, and Shen Yan.

sentences.zh: 累遷晉熙王安西司馬，加甯朔將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Pacifying West Army Major on Prince Jinxi's staff, with the added title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Pacifying West Army Major on Prince Jinxi's staff and was given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 時齊武帝為長史，與世隆相遇甚歡。

translations.literal: At that time the future Qi Emperor Wu was chief clerk, and he and Shilong met with great mutual delight.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Wu of Qi was then chief clerk on the staff, and he and Shilong became fast friends.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝之謀度廣陵也，令武帝率眾同會都下。

translations.literal: When the future Qi Emperor Gao plotted to measure Guangling, he ordered Emperor Wu to lead troops to rendezvous at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi was planning his move against Guangling, he ordered the future Emperor Wu to bring troops to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世隆與長流參軍蕭景先等戒嚴待期，事不行。

translations.literal: Shilong with Chief Clerk Xiao Jingxian and others stood on alert awaiting the date, but the affair did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong, Xiao Jingxian, and others stood ready on alert, but the plot never came off.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷疑憚沈攸之，密為之防，府州器械，皆有素蓄。

translations.literal: At that time the court feared Shen Youzhi and secretly made preparations against him; prefectural and provincial armaments were all stored in advance.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared Shen Youzhi and quietly laid plans against him; arms and stores were laid up throughout the provinces.

sentences.zh: 武帝將下都，劉懷珍白高帝曰：「夏口是兵沖要地，宜得其人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was about to go down to the capital, Liu Huaizhen reported to Emperor Gao: "Xiakou is a vital military crossroads; it should have the right man."
translations.idiomatic: As the future Emperor Wu prepared to go to the capital, Liu Huaizhen told Emperor Gao: "Xiakou is a critical military point and needs the right commander."

sentences.zh: 」高帝納之，與武帝書曰：「汝既入朝，當須文武兼資人，委以後事，世隆其人也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao accepted this and wrote to Emperor Wu: "Since you are entering court, you need a man of both civil and military talent to entrust with later affairs—Shilong is that man."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao agreed and wrote to the future Emperor Wu: "Once you reach the capital you will need a man of both civil and military gifts to hold the rear—Shilong is the man."

sentences.zh: 」武帝乃舉世隆自代。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu thereupon recommended Shilong to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Wu then nominated Shilong as his replacement.

sentences.zh: 轉為武陵王前軍長史、江夏內史，行郢州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Vanguard Army on Prince Wuling's staff, Interior Minister of Jiangxia, and acting Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk of the vanguard on Prince Wuling's staff, made Interior Minister of Jiangxia, and given acting charge of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 武帝初下，與世隆別，曰：「攸之一旦為變，雖留攻城，不可卒拔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu first went down, he parted from Shilong and said: "If Youzhi rebels at once, though he may leave troops to besiege the city, it cannot be taken quickly.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu first marched east, he took leave of Shilong and said: "If Youzhi rebels, he may leave men to besiege your city, but he cannot take it in haste.

sentences.zh: 卿為其內，我為其外，乃無憂耳。

translations.literal: You will be inside, I outside—then there will be no worry."
translations.idiomatic: You hold the inside, I the outside, and we need not fear."

sentences.zh: 」至是，武帝遣軍主桓敬、陳胤叔、苟元賓等八軍據西塞，令堅壁以待賊疲。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Wu sent army commanders Huan Jing, Chen Yingshu, Gou Yuanbin, and eight armies to hold Xisai, ordering them to strengthen their walls and wait for the enemy to tire.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Wu then sent eight armies under Huan Jing, Chen Yingshu, Gou Yuanbin, and others to hold Xisai, with orders to stand on the defensive until the rebels wore themselves out.

sentences.zh: 慮世隆危急，遣腹心胡元直潛使入郢城通援軍消息。

translations.literal: Fearing Shilong was in peril, he sent his trusted man Hu Yuanzhi secretly into Ying city to convey news of relief forces.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for Shilong, he sent his trusted agent Hu Yuanzhi secretly into Ying city with word of the relief armies.

sentences.zh: 內外並喜。

translations.literal: Inside and outside alike rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison and relief force alike took heart.

sentences.zh: 郢城既不可攻，而平西將軍黃回軍至西陽，乘三層艦，作羌胡伎，泝流而進。

translations.literal: Since Ying city could not be taken, Pacifying West General Huang Hui's army reached Xiyang, riding triple-deck ships, performing Qiang and Hu entertainments, and advancing upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Ying city still could not be stormed when Pacifying West General Huang Hui reached Xiyang with triple-deck warships, barbarian music playing at the prows, rowing upstream.

sentences.zh: 攸之素失人情，本逼以威力，初發江陵，已有叛者，至此稍多。

translations.literal: Youzhi had long lost men's hearts; he had originally relied on brute force; when he first set out from Jiangling there were already deserters, and by now there were somewhat more.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi had never won men's loyalty and ruled by fear alone; deserters had appeared from the day he left Jiangling, and their numbers were growing.

sentences.zh: 攸之大怒，於是一人叛，遣十人追，並去不返。

translations.literal: Youzhi was greatly enraged; thus when one man deserted he sent ten to pursue, and they all left and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi flew into a rage: for every deserter he sent ten men in pursuit, and the pursuers deserted as well.

sentences.zh: 劉攘兵射書與世隆請降，開門納之。

translations.literal: Liu Rangbing shot a letter to Shilong offering surrender, and opened the gate to admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rangbing sent a message offering surrender to Shilong and opened the gates to him.

sentences.zh: 攸之怒，銜須咀之，收攘兵兄子天賜、女婿張平慮斬之。

translations.literal: Youzhi in anger bit his beard and chewed it; he seized Rangbing's elder brother's son Tiansi and son-in-law Zhang Pinglu and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi gnawed his beard in fury, seized Rangbing's nephew Tiansi and son-in-law Zhang Pinglu, and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 軍旅大散。

translations.literal: The army and host scattered on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: His army broke apart completely.

sentences.zh: 世隆乃遣軍副劉僧麟緣道追之。

translations.literal: Shilong then sent Army Deputy Liu Senglin to pursue along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong sent Army Deputy Liu Senglin in pursuit along the road.

sentences.zh: 攸之已死，徵為侍中，仍遷尚書右僕射，封貞陽縣侯。

translations.literal: After Youzhi was dead, Shilong was summoned as Palace Attendant, then transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Imperial Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhenyang County.
translations.idiomatic: After Youzhi's death Shilong was recalled as Palace Attendant, promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhenyang.

sentences.zh: 出為吳郡太守，居母憂，寒不衣絮。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Wu Commandery; in mourning for his mother, in cold weather he wore no padded garments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Wu Commandery; during his mother's mourning he would not wear padded clothes even in the cold.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝踐阼，起為南豫州刺史，加都督，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Qi Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Shilong was recalled as Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, with added command authority, and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi took the throne, Shilong was recalled as Inspector of Southern Yu Province with full military authority and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 上手詔司徒褚彥回甚傷美之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally issued an edict to Minister of Works Chu Yanhui greatly praising his beauty of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote to Minister of Works Chu Yanhui praising Shilong in the highest terms.

sentences.zh: 彥回曰：「世隆事陛下，在危盡忠，居憂杖而後起，立人之本，二理同極，加榮增寵，足以敦厲風俗。」

translations.literal: Yanhui said: "Shilong in serving Your Majesty was utterly loyal in peril, and in mourning used the staff before rising—both reach the root of establishing men; to add honor and increase favor is enough to encourage and strengthen custom."
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui replied: "In serving Your Majesty Shilong was utterly loyal in danger and observed mourning to the letter—both are the stuff of true manhood. To honor him further would strengthen the moral tone of the realm."

sentences.zh: 建元二年，授右僕射，不拜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan he was appointed Vice Director of the Right but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan he was offered the vice directorship of the Secretariat but declined.

sentences.zh: 性愛涉獵，啟高帝借秘閣書，上給二千卷。

translations.literal: By nature he loved wide reading; he petitioned Emperor Gao to borrow books from the secret archive, and the emperor gave him two thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning for its own sake and asked Emperor Gao for books from the imperial archive; the emperor lent him two thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 三年，出為南兗州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, with added command authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was posted as Inspector of Southern Yan Province with full military authority.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was given the added title Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu acceded, Shilong was made Attendant Cavalier as well.

sentences.zh: 世隆善卜，別龜甲，價至一萬。

translations.literal: Shilong was skilled in divination; a special tortoise shell of his fetched up to ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was skilled in divination; one of his special tortoise shells was valued at ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 永明初，世隆曰：「永明九年我亡，亡後三年丘山崩，齊亦于此季矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming, Shilong said: "In the ninth year of Yongming I shall die; three years after my death the hills will collapse, and Qi too will end in that season."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongming he said: "I shall die in the ninth year of Yongming; three years later the imperial tombs will fall, and Qi will perish in that same season."

sentences.zh: 」屏人，命典簽李黨取筆及高齒屐，題簾箔旌曰：「永明十一年。

translations.literal: He dismissed attendants, ordered Chief Clerk Li Dang to bring brush and high-toothed clogs, and inscribed on curtain foil and banner: "The eleventh year of Yongming."
translations.idiomatic: Sending everyone away, he had Chief Clerk Li Dang bring brush and clogs and wrote on a curtain and banner: "The eleventh year of Yongming."

sentences.zh: 」因流涕謂黨曰：「汝當見，吾不見也。

translations.literal: He then wept and said to Dang: "You will see it; I will not."
translations.idiomatic: With tears he told Dang: "You will live to see it; I shall not."

sentences.zh: 」遷護軍，而衛軍王儉修下官敬甚謹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial Guards, while Guards General Wang Jian observed the courtesy due a subordinate with great care.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Imperial Guards; Guards General Wang Jian paid him the full ceremonial deference owed a superior.

sentences.zh: 世隆止之，儉曰：「將軍雖存弘眷，如王典何。

translations.literal: Shilong stopped him; Jian said: "Though the general shows generous regard, what of the royal statutes?"
translations.idiomatic: Shilong tried to stop him; Jian said: "Your kindness is generous, General, but what of the court ritual?"

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which men held him.

sentences.zh: 性清廉，唯盛事墳典。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and incorrupt; he honored only the classics of the tombs and archives.
translations.idiomatic: He was incorrupt by nature and cared only for books and learning.

sentences.zh: 張緒問曰：「觀君舉措，當以清名遺子孫邪？

translations.literal: Zhang Xu asked: "Judging from your conduct, do you intend to bequeath a pure reputation to your descendants?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu asked him: "From your way of living, are you leaving your sons nothing but a name for integrity?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「一身之外，亦復何須。

translations.literal: He answered: "Beyond one's own person, what further need is there?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Beyond this single life, what do we need?"

sentences.zh: 子孫不才，將為爭府；

translations.literal: If descendants lack talent, they will fight over the household;
translations.idiomatic: If my sons lack talent, they will squabble over the estate;

sentences.zh: 如其才也，不如一經。」

translations.literal: if they have talent, one classic is better."
translations.idiomatic: if they have talent, one classic is worth more than any fortune."

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫韋祖征州裏宿德，世隆雖已貴重，每為之拜。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Wei Zuzheng was an elder of virtue in the province; though Shilong was already eminent, he always bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zuzheng, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, was a revered elder of the region; though already a great minister, Shilong always bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 人或勸祖征止之，答曰：「司馬公所為，後生楷法，吾豈能止之哉。

translations.literal: Some urged Zuzheng to stop this; he answered: "What the Lord Marshal does is a model for the young—how could I stop it?"
translations.idiomatic: When others urged Zuzheng to accept less deference, he said: "What the Marshal does is an example for the young—how could I forbid it?"

sentences.zh: 」後授尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Vice Director of the Left in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 湘州蠻動，遣世隆以本官總督伐蠻眾軍，仍為湘州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When the Man of Xiangzhou stirred, Shilong was sent with his existing rank to command all armies suppressing the Man, and concurrently made Inspector of Xiangzhou with command authority.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Xiang Province rebelled, Shilong was sent to command all punitive forces, made Inspector of Xiang Province, and given full military authority.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，以方略討平之。

translations.literal: On reaching his post, he pacified them by strategy.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he pacified them by strategy.

sentences.zh: 在州立邸興生，為御史中丞庾杲之所奏。

translations.literal: In the province he established lodges for trade, and was impeached by Imperial Censor Yuan Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He set up trading lodges in the province and was impeached by Imperial Censor Yuan Gao.

sentences.zh: 詔不問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the charge dropped.

sentences.zh: 復入為尚書左僕射，不拜，乃轉尚書令。

translations.literal: He returned as Vice Director of the Left but did not accept, and was then transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Vice Director of the Secretariat, he declined and was made Director instead.

sentences.zh: 世隆少立功名，晚專以談義自業。

translations.literal: Shilong in youth established merit and fame; in later years he devoted himself solely to pure talk and doctrine as his profession.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong had won fame in youth by arms; in later years he devoted himself to pure talk and scholarship.

sentences.zh: 善彈琴，世稱柳公雙瑣，為士品第一。

translations.literal: He was skilled at playing the zither; the age called him Lord Liu's Twin Locks, ranked first among gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He was a master of the zither; men called his instrument "Lord Liu's Twin Locks" and ranked his playing first among scholars.

sentences.zh: 常自云：「馬矟第一，清談第二，彈琴第三。

translations.literal: He often said himself: "With the cavalry lance I am first, in pure talk second, in zither third."
translations.idiomatic: He used to say: "First with the lance, second in pure talk, third at the zither."

sentences.zh: 」在朝不幹世務，垂簾鼓琴，風韻清遠，甚獲世譽。

translations.literal: At court he did not meddle in worldly affairs; behind drawn curtains he played the zither—his bearing clear and far-reaching, and he won great praise from the age.
translations.idiomatic: At court he kept clear of routine business, played the zither behind drawn curtains, and won wide praise for his refined, distant air.

sentences.zh: 以疾遜位，拜左光祿大夫、侍中。

translations.literal: Because of illness he yielded his post and was appointed Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to step down; he was named Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 永明九年卒，詔給東園秘器，贈司空，班劍二十人，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth year of Yongming; an edict granted Eastern Garden secret rites, posthumous Minister of Works, twenty halberd-bearing guards, and the posthumous title Loyal Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Yongming; the court granted imperial funeral rites, posthumously named him Minister of Works with twenty ceremonial guards, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal Martial.

sentences.zh: 世隆曉數術，于倪塘創墓，與賓客踐履，十往五往，常坐一處。

translations.literal: Shilong understood numerology; at Nitang he created a tomb and with guests walked the ground—five times in ten he would sit in one place.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong understood divination; at Nitang he laid out a tomb site and walked the ground with guests, often sitting in the same spot five times out of ten.

sentences.zh: 及卒，墓工圖墓，正取其坐處焉。

translations.literal: When he died, the tomb craftsmen drew the tomb plan and took exactly the place where he had sat.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the tomb builders set the grave exactly where he had so often sat.

sentences.zh: 所著龜經秘要二卷，行於世。

translations.literal: His authored Secret Essentials of the Tortoise Classic in two scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His two-scroll Secret Essentials of the Tortoise Classic circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 長子悅字文殊，少有清致，位中書郎，早卒，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yue, style name Wenshu, in youth had pure refinement; he held the post of Secretariat Gentleman, died young, and was posthumously titled Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yue, styled Wenshu, showed refined taste from youth, served as Secretariat Gentleman, died young, and received the posthumous title Reverent.

sentences.zh: 世隆次子惔。

translations.literal: Shilong's second son Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's second son was Tan.

sentences.zh: 惔字文通，好學工制文，尤曉音律，少與長兄悅齊名。

translations.literal: Tan, style name Wentong, loved learning and was skilled at regulated prose, especially understood musical pitch and law; in youth he and elder brother Yue were equally famous.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, styled Wentong, loved learning and excelled at literary composition and music theory; in youth he shared equal fame with his elder brother Yue.

sentences.zh: 王儉謂人曰：「柳氏二龍，可謂一日千里。

translations.literal: Wang Jian said to others: "The two dragons of the Liu clan can truly cover a thousand li in a day."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian said of them: "The Liu family's two dragons cover a thousand li in a single day."

sentences.zh: 」儉為尚書左僕射，嘗造世隆宅，世隆謂為詣己，徘徊久之。

translations.literal: Jian was Vice Director of the Left; once he visited Shilong's residence, and Shilong thought the visit was for himself and paced about for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian, as Vice Director of the Secretariat, once called at Shilong's house, Shilong assumed the visit was for him and waited a long while.

sentences.zh: 及至門，唯求悅及惔。

translations.literal: When he reached the gate, he sought only Yue and Tan.
translations.idiomatic: At the gate Jian asked only for Yue and Tan.

sentences.zh: 遣謂世隆曰：「賢子俱有盛才，一日見顧，今故報禮。

translations.literal: He sent word to Shilong: "Your worthy sons both have splendid talent; I paid them a visit one day, and now return the courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Shilong: "Your sons are both gifted; I called on them the other day and now return the courtesy."

sentences.zh: 若仍相造，似非本意，恐年少窺人。」

translations.literal: If I visit again, it would seem not my true intent, and I fear the young will spy on people's motives."
translations.idiomatic: Further visits might look like something else, and the young are quick to read men's motives."

sentences.zh: 嘗預齊武烽火樓宴，帝善其詩，謂豫章王嶷曰：「惔非徒風韻清爽，亦屬文遒麗。

translations.literal: Once at Emperor Wu of Qi's Beacon Tower banquet, the emperor praised his poetry and said to Prince Yuzhang Nian: "Tan is not only clear and refreshing in bearing—his writing is also forceful and beautiful."
translations.idiomatic: At a Beacon Tower banquet under the future Emperor Wu of Qi, the prince praised Tan's poetry and told Prince of Yuzhang: "Tan is not only graceful in manner—his writing is vigorous and fine."

sentences.zh: 」後為巴東王子響友，子響為荊州，惔隨之鎮。

translations.literal: Later he became companion to Prince Zixiang of Badong; when Zixiang held Jingzhou, Tan followed him to the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He later became companion to Prince Zixiang of Badong and accompanied him when Zixiang was posted to Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 子響昵近小人，惔知將為禍，稱疾還都。

translations.literal: Zixiang was intimate with petty men; Tan knew disaster would come, feigned illness, and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang kept company with worthless men; Tan foresaw disaster, pleaded illness, and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及難作竟以得免。

translations.literal: When the calamity occurred he escaped in the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis broke he alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 累遷新安太守，居郡以無政績免。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Xin'an; while in the commandery he was dismissed for lack of administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of Xin'an but was dismissed for achieving nothing in office.

sentences.zh: 建武末，為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwu he was Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianwu era he was Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 及梁武帝起兵，惔舉漢中以應。

translations.literal: When Liang Emperor Wu raised troops, Tan raised Hanzhong in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised his banner, Tan rallied Hanzhong to his cause.

sentences.zh: 梁武受命，為太子詹事，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Liang Wu received the Mandate, Tan was made Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the added title Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang founder took the throne, Tan was made Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 武帝之鎮襄陽，惔祖道，帝解茅土玉環贈之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was stationed at Xiangyang, Tan gave him a farewell feast; the emperor removed a jade ring from his girdle and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the future emperor was posted to Xiangyang, Tan gave him a farewell feast and received a jade ring from his belt in return.

sentences.zh: 天監二年元會，帝謂曰：「卿所佩玉環，是新亭所贈邪？

translations.literal: At the New Year's assembly in the second year of Tianjian, the emperor said: "The jade ring you wear—is it the one given at Xinting?"
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year's court in the second year of Tianjian, the emperor asked: "The jade ring at your belt—is that the one from our farewell at Xinting?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「既而瑞感神衷，臣謹服之無斁。

translations.literal: He answered: "Then an auspicious sign moved the divine heart; your servant respectfully wears it without weariness."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "A blessed omen touched the divine heart; I wear it ever in gratitude."

sentences.zh: 」帝因勸之酒，惔時未卒爵，帝曰：「吾常比卿劉越石，近辭卮酒邪。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon urged him to drink; Tan had not yet finished his cup when the emperor said: "I often compare you to Liu Yueshi—are you lately declining the wine cup?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed wine on him; Tan had not drained his cup when the emperor said: "I have often likened you to Liu Yueshi—will you refuse the cup now?"

sentences.zh: 」罷會，封曲江縣侯。

translations.literal: When the assembly ended, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang County.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended, Tan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 帝因宴為詩貽惔曰：「爾實冠群後，惟餘實念功。

translations.literal: At a banquet the emperor composed a poem and presented it to Tan, saying: "You truly crown all the rest; only I truly remember your merit."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the emperor wrote him a poem: "You stand first among them all; I alone keep your service in mind."

sentences.zh: 」帝又嘗謂曰：「徐元瑜違命嶺南，周書父子兄弟罪不相及，朕已放其諸子，何如？

translations.literal: The emperor also once said: "Xu Yuanyu defied orders in Lingnan; the Book of Zhou says guilt does not extend between fathers and sons or brothers—I have already released his sons. What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked him: "Xu Yuanyu rebelled in the far south; the Zhou canon says that guilt does not chain from father to son or brother to brother. I have released his sons—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」惔曰：「罰

translations.literal: Tan said: "Punishment
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "Punishment

sentences.zh: 不及嗣，賞延於後，今復見之聖朝。

translations.literal: does not reach descendants; reward extends to posterity—today we see this again in the holy court."
translations.idiomatic: does not reach the sons; reward flows to posterity—we see that principle alive again in this sacred court."

sentences.zh: 」時以為知言。

translations.literal: The age considered this wise speech.
translations.idiomatic: Men at the time praised his answer as wise.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書左僕射，年四十六，卒于湘州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Left in the Imperial Secretariat; at age forty-six he died while Inspector of Xiangzhou, and was posthumously titled Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Director of the Secretariat; he died at forty-six while serving as Inspector of Xiang Province and received the posthumous title Reverent.

sentences.zh: 惔度量寬博，家人未嘗見其喜慍。

translations.literal: Tan was broad in measure; his household never saw him pleased or angry.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was magnanimous by nature; his family never saw him show pleasure or anger.

sentences.zh: 甚重其婦，頗成畏憚。

translations.literal: He greatly respected his wife and came to fear and defer to her.
translations.idiomatic: He held his wife in high regard and stood somewhat in awe of her.

sentences.zh: 性愛音樂，女伎精麗，略不敢視。

translations.literal: By nature he loved music, but the female performers were refined and beautiful, and he scarcely dared look at them.
translations.idiomatic: He loved music by nature, yet the female performers were so lovely that he scarcely dared glance at them.

sentences.zh: 僕射張稷與惔狎密，而為惔妻賞敬。

translations.literal: Vice Director Zhang Ji was intimate with Tan, yet was admired and respected by Tan's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Zhang Ji was on close terms with Tan, yet Tan's wife admired and respected him.

sentences.zh: 稷每詣惔，必先相問夫人。

translations.literal: Whenever Ji visited Tan, he always first inquired after the lady.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Ji called on Tan, he always asked first after Tan's wife.

sentences.zh: 惔每欲見妓，恒因稷請奏。

translations.literal: Whenever Tan wished to see the performers, he always had Ji request a performance.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan wished to hear the performers, he always had Ji ask for a performance.

sentences.zh: 其妻隔幔坐，妓然後出。

translations.literal: His wife sat behind a curtain; only then did the performers come out.
translations.idiomatic: His wife sat behind a curtain, and only then would the performers appear.

sentences.zh: 惔因得留目。

translations.literal: Tan thereby could linger his gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Only then could Tan steal a lingering look.

sentences.zh: 惔著仁政傳及諸詩賦，粗有辭義。

translations.literal: Tan authored a Record of Benevolent Government and various poems and rhapsodies, with some literary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tan wrote a Treatise on Benevolent Government and various poems and fu, all with respectable literary merit.

sentences.zh: 子昭，位中書郎，襲爵曲江侯。

translations.literal: His son Zhao held the post of Secretariat Gentleman and inherited the title Marquis of Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao served as Secretariat Gentleman and inherited the marquisate of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 惔弟惲字文暢，少有志行。

translations.literal: Tan's younger brother Yun, style name Wenchang, in youth had aspiration and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's younger brother Yun, styled Wenchang, showed purpose and integrity from youth.

sentences.zh: 好學，善尺牘。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at letters.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and wrote excellent letters.

sentences.zh: 與陳郡謝淪鄰居，深見友愛。

translations.literal: He was neighbor to Xie Lun of Chen Commandery, and they deeply befriended one another.
translations.idiomatic: He lived next to Xie Lun of Chen Commandery, and they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 淪曰：「宅南柳郎，可為儀錶。」

translations.literal: Lun said: "Young Lord Liu south of the residence can serve as a model."
translations.idiomatic: Lun said: "The young Liu south of our houses could be a model for any man."

sentences.zh: 初，宋時有嵇元榮、羊蓋者，並善琴，雲傳戴安道法。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Song times there were Ji Yuanrong and Yang Gai, both skilled at the zither, said to transmit the method of Dai Andao.
translations.idiomatic: In Song times Ji Yuanrong and Yang Gai were both master zither players, said to carry on the tradition of Dai Andao.

sentences.zh: 惲從之學。

translations.literal: Yun studied under them.
translations.idiomatic: Yun studied under them.

sentences.zh: 惲特窮其妙。

translations.literal: Yun especially exhausted their subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Yun mastered their art to its depths.

sentences.zh: 齊竟陵王子良聞而引為法曹行參軍，唯與王暕、陸杲善。

translations.literal: Qi Prince Ziliang of Jingling heard of this and brought him in as Acting Army Controller in the Law Bureau; he was friendly only with Wang Yan and Lu Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling heard of him and made him acting legal officer on his staff; his only close friends were Wang Yan and Lu Gao.

sentences.zh: 每歎曰：「暕雖名家，猶恐累我也。

translations.literal: He often sighed: "Though Yan is of an eminent house, I still fear he may drag me down."
translations.idiomatic: He would sigh: "Even Wang Yan, for all his great family, might still weigh me down."

sentences.zh: 」雅被子良賞狎。

translations.literal: He was always prized and treated familiarly by Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang always favored and indulged him.

sentences.zh: 子良嘗置酒後園，有晉太傅謝安鳴琴在側，援以授惲，惲彈為雅弄。

translations.literal: Ziliang once set wine in the rear garden; a zither that had belonged to Jin Grand Tutor Xie An was at hand, and he handed it to Yun, who played an elegant piece.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang once gave a feast in his rear garden; a zither once owned by Grand Tutor Xie An of Jin lay nearby, and he gave it to Yun, who played an elegant air.

sentences.zh: 子良曰：「卿巧越嵇心，妙臻羊體，良質美手，信在今夜。

translations.literal: Ziliang said: "Your skill surpasses Ji's heart, your subtlety reaches Yang's body—fine timber and beautiful hands, truly in this night."
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang said: "Your art surpasses Ji's soul and matches Yang's style—fine wood and gifted hands, all proved tonight."

sentences.zh: 豈止當今稱奇，亦可追蹤古烈。」

translations.literal: This is not only to be called marvelous in the present age—you may also follow the traces of ancient worthies."
translations.idiomatic: You are not merely the wonder of our age—you may stand with the masters of old."

sentences.zh: 為太子洗馬，父憂去官，著述先頌，申其罔極之心，文甚哀麗。

translations.literal: He was Palace Groom for the Heir Apparent; on his father's death he left office, composed a eulogy for his forebear, expressing his boundless heart—the writing was very mournful and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Palace Groom to the Heir Apparent; when his father died he left office and wrote a funeral hymn of deep grief, moving and beautiful in its language.

sentences.zh: 後試守鄱陽相，聽吏屬得盡三年喪禮，署之文教，百姓稱焉。

translations.literal: Later he was tried as Administrator of Poyang; he allowed clerks and subordinates to complete the three-year mourning rites, and in his appointments emphasized culture and teaching—the common people praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as acting Administrator of Poyang, allowed his staff the full three years of mourning, and filled his appointments with men of learning; the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 還除驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made Attendant Gentleman on the staff of the General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝至建鄴，惲候謁石頭，以為征東府司馬。

translations.literal: When Liang Emperor Wu reached Jiankang, Yun waited to pay respects at Shitou and was made Eastern Campaigning Army Major.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang reached Jiankang, Yun met him at Shitou and was appointed major on the Eastern Campaigning Army staff.

sentences.zh: 上箋請城平之日，先收圖籍，及遵漢高寬大之義。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial asking that on the day the city was pacified, registers and archives be secured first, and that the broad and generous principle of Han Emperor Gao be followed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that when the city fell, the archives should be secured first and that the conquerors should follow the magnanimous example of Emperor Gao of Han.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 徙為相國右司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Major of the Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Major on the Chancellor of State's staff.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，除長兼侍中，與僕射沈約等共定新律。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was appointed Chief Concurrent Palace Attendant, and with Vice Director Shen Yue and others jointly fixed the new code.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian he was made Chief Concurrent Palace Attendant and, with Vice Director Shen Yue and others, helped draft the new legal code.

sentences.zh: 惲立性貞素，以貴公子早有令名，少工篇什，為詩云：「亭皋木葉下，壟首秋雲飛。

translations.literal: Yun's nature was upright and plain; as a nobleman's son he early had a fine reputation; in youth he was skilled at verse, composing a poem: "On the terrace the tree leaves fall; above the mound autumn clouds fly."
translations.idiomatic: Yun was upright and unadorned by nature; as a young nobleman he won early fame for poetry, including the lines: "Leaves fall on the terrace; autumn clouds drift above the mound."

sentences.zh: 」琅邪王融見而嗟賞，因書齋壁及所執白團扇。

translations.literal: Wang Rong of Langye saw it and sighed in admiration, and therefore wrote it on his study wall and on the white round fan he held.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong of Langye admired it and copied the lines on his study wall and on his white silk fan.

sentences.zh: 武帝與宴，必詔惲賦詩。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Wu feasted with him, he always ordered Yun to compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor feasted with him, he ordered Yun to compose a poem.

sentences.zh: 嘗和武帝登景陽樓篇云：太液滄波起，長楊高樹秋，翠華承漢遠，雕輦逐風遊。

translations.literal: Once, responding to the emperor's piece on ascending Jingyang Tower, he wrote: "Great Pool's dark waves rise; tall poplars, high trees in autumn; emerald banners receive the Han afar; carved chariots chase the wind in roaming."
translations.idiomatic: Once, matching the emperor's poem on ascending Jingyang Tower, he wrote: "Dark waves rise on the Great Pool; tall poplars mark the autumn air; imperial banners greet the distant Han; carved carriages ride the wind."

sentences.zh: 」深見賞美。

translations.literal: He was deeply admired and praised.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired it greatly.

sentences.zh: 當時咸共稱傳。

translations.literal: At the time all together praised and circulated it.
translations.idiomatic: The poem was praised and passed around at court.

sentences.zh: 曆平越中郎將、廣州刺史，秘書監，右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of General of the Pacifying Yue Interior Army, Inspector of Guangzhou, Director of the Secretariat, and General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as General of the Pacifying Yue Interior Army, Inspector of Guang Province, Director of the Secretariat, and General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 再為吳興太守，為政清靜，人吏懷之。

translations.literal: He twice served as Administrator of Wuxing; his governance was pure and quiet, and officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he governed Wuxing with quiet integrity, and officials and people alike held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 于郡感疾，自陳解任。

translations.literal: In the commandery he fell ill and himself petitioned to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill in office and asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 父老千餘

translations.literal: More than a thousand elders
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand elders

sentences.zh: 人拜表陳請，事未施行，卒。

translations.literal: bowed in memorial petition; before the matter could be carried out, he died.
translations.idiomatic: submitted a joint petition begging him to stay; before the request could be granted, he died.

sentences.zh: 初，惲父世隆彈琴，為士流第一，惲每奏其父曲，常感思。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yun's father Shilong played the zither and was first among gentlemen; whenever Yun played his father's pieces, he was often moved to reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's father Shilong had been the finest zither player of his generation; when Yun played his father's music, he was often overcome with feeling.

sentences.zh: 復變體備寫古曲。

translations.literal: He also varied the forms and fully transcribed ancient pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He also reworked old forms and set down ancient pieces in full.

sentences.zh: 嘗賦詩未就，以筆捶琴，坐客過，以箸扣之，惲驚其哀韻，乃制為雅音。

translations.literal: Once, while composing a poem that was not yet finished, he tapped the zither with his brush; a seated guest passed by and struck it with chopsticks—Yun was startled by the mournful tone and fashioned it into an elegant piece.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while struggling with a poem, he struck the zither with his brush; a guest rapped it with chopsticks as he passed, and Yun, struck by the plaintive note, turned it into a refined composition.

sentences.zh: 後傳擊琴自於此。
