translations.literal: Later the tradition of striking the zither began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition of struck-zither music began with this incident.

sentences.zh: 惲常以今聲轉棄古法，乃著清調論，具有條流。

translations.literal: Yun often used present sounds and turned away from ancient methods; he therefore authored a Treatise on Pure Tones, fully ordered in sections.
translations.idiomatic: Yun often favored contemporary sounds over ancient methods and wrote a Treatise on Pure Tones, arranged in clear sections.

sentences.zh: 齊竟陵王嘗宿晏，明旦將朝見，惲投壺梟不絕，停輿久之，進見遂晚。

translations.literal: Qi Prince Ziliang of Jingling once lodged at Yan; the next dawn he was to attend court audience—Yun played pitch-pot without cease, and the carriage halted a long while; entering audience was thus late.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling once stayed overnight at Yan; the next morning he was due at court, but Yun kept him playing pitch-pot, the carriage waited a long while, and the prince arrived late.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝遲之，王以實對。

translations.literal: Qi Emperor Wu was displeased at the delay; the prince answered with the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi was annoyed at the delay; the prince told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 武帝復使為之，賜絹二十匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had him do it again and bestowed twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Yun play again and rewarded him with twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 嘗與琅邪王瞻博射，嫌其皮闊，乃摘梅帖烏珠之上，發必命中，觀者驚駭。

translations.literal: Once he competed in archery with Wang Zhan of Langye; finding the target hide too wide, he plucked plum blossoms and fixed them on the black pearl center—every shot hit, and onlookers were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Once, shooting against Wang Zhan of Langye, he found the target too large, plucked plum blossoms and fixed them on the bull's-eye, and never missed; the spectators were astounded.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝好弈棋，使惲品定棋譜，登格者二百七十八人，第其優劣，為棋品三卷。

translations.literal: Liang Emperor Wu loved weiqi; he had Yun grade the chess registers—two hundred seventy-eight men qualified—and rank their superiority and inferiority, producing Chess Ranks in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang loved weiqi and had Yun rank the players; two hundred seventy-eight qualified, and Yun graded them in three scrolls of Chess Ranks.

sentences.zh: 惲為第二焉。

translations.literal: Yun ranked second.
translations.idiomatic: Yun himself ranked second.

sentences.zh: 帝謂周舍曰：「吾聞君子不可求備，至如柳惲可謂具美。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zhou She: "I have heard that a gentleman cannot be required to be complete—but as for Liu Yun, he may be called fully accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Zhou She: "They say no man can be perfect in everything—yet Liu Yun comes as close as anyone.

sentences.zh: 分其才藝，足了十人。

translations.literal: Divide his talents and arts, and they would suffice for ten men."
translations.idiomatic: Split his talents among ten men, and each would still be accomplished."

sentences.zh: 」惲著卜杖龜經。

translations.literal: Yun authored the Tortoise Classic of the Divining Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yun wrote the Tortoise Classic of the Divining Staff.

sentences.zh: 性好醫術，盡其精妙。

translations.literal: By nature he loved medical arts and exhausted their subtle mastery.
translations.idiomatic: He loved medicine and mastered it to its finest points.

sentences.zh: 少子偃字彥遊，年十二，梁武帝引見，詔問讀何書，對曰：「尚書。

translations.literal: His youngest son Yan, style name Yanyou, at age twelve was summoned by Liang Emperor Wu; the emperor asked what book he read, and he answered: "The Documents."
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Yan, styled Yanyou, at twelve was presented to Emperor Wu, who asked what he was reading; the boy answered: "The Book of Documents."

sentences.zh: 」又問有何美句，對曰：「德惟善政，政在養人。

translations.literal: He was again asked what fine lines it had; he answered: "Virtue is good government; government lies in nourishing the people."
translations.idiomatic: Asked for a fine passage, he quoted: "Virtue is good government, and government lies in nourishing the people."

sentences.zh: 」眾咸異之。

translations.literal: All present were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present was astonished.

sentences.zh: 詔尚武帝女長城公主，拜駙馬都尉、都亭侯，位鄱陽內史，卒。

translations.literal: An edict married him to Emperor Wu's daughter Princess Changcheng; he was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards and Marquis of Duting, held the post of Interior Minister of Poyang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was married to the emperor's daughter Princess Changcheng, made Commandant of the Horse Guards and Marquis of Duting, served as Interior Minister of Poyang, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 後從祖弟莊清警有鑒識，自盼卒後，太后宗屬唯莊為近，兼素有名望，深被恩禮。

translations.literal: A later second cousin Zhuang was clear, alert, and discerning; after Pan's death, among the empress dowager's clan Zhuang alone was nearest, and he also had long-standing fame and was deeply favored with grace and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: A later kinsman Zhuang was acute and discerning; after Pan's death he was the empress dowager's closest male relative, long respected at court and deeply honored.

sentences.zh: 位度支尚書。

translations.literal: He held the post of Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，為岐州司馬。

translations.literal: When Chen perished he entered Sui and was made Military Aide of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell he entered Sui service as Military Aide of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 惲弟憕。

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's younger brother was Chen.

sentences.zh: 憕字文深，少有大意，好玄言，通老、易。

translations.literal: Chen, style name Wenshen, in youth had great purpose; he loved arcane discourse and was versed in the Laozi and Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, styled Wenshen, was ambitious from youth, loved philosophical discourse, and mastered the Laozi and Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝舉兵至姑孰，憕與兄惲及諸友朋于小郊候接。

translations.literal: When Liang Emperor Wu raised troops to Gushu, Chen with his elder brother Yun and various friends waited to receive him in the outer suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang marched to Gushu, Chen joined his brother Yun and their friends to welcome him in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 時道路猶梗，憕與諸人同憩逆旅食，俱去行里餘，憕曰：「寧我負人，不人負我。

translations.literal: The roads were still blocked; Chen and the others together rested at an inn to eat, and all went more than a li—Chen said: "Better that I wrong others than that others wrong me.
translations.idiomatic: The roads were still unsafe; after eating at an inn they had gone a little over a li when Chen said: "Better that I wrong others than that others wrong me.

sentences.zh: 若復有追，堪憩此客。

translations.literal: If there is pursuit again, this inn can shelter them."
translations.idiomatic: If pursuers come again, let them rest at this inn."

sentences.zh: 」命左右燒逆旅舍，以絕後追。

translations.literal: He ordered attendants to burn the inn, to cut off pursuit from behind.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to burn the inn to block pursuit from behind.

sentences.zh: 當時服其善斷。

translations.literal: At the time men admired his decisive judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Men at the time admired his decisive judgment.

sentences.zh: 歷位給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively held the post of Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 與琅邪王峻齊名，俱為中庶子，時人號為方王。

translations.literal: He was equally famous with Wang Jun of Langye; both were Palace Companions, and men of the time called them the Square Wangs.
translations.idiomatic: He shared equal fame with Wang Jun of Langye; both were Palace Companions, and contemporaries called them the Two Wangs.

sentences.zh: 後為鎮北始興王長史。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief Clerk on Prince Shixing's Pacifying North staff.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief clerk to Prince Shixing of Pacifying North.

sentences.zh: 王移鎮益州，復請憕。

translations.literal: When the prince moved his garrison to Yizhou, he again requested Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was transferred to Yi Province, he asked for Chen again.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「柳憕風標才氣，恐不能久為少王臣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Liu Chen's bearing and talent—I fear he cannot long remain a young prince's subject."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Liu Chen's talent and presence are too great to keep long in a prince's service."

sentences.zh: 」王祈請數四，不得已，以為鎮西長史、蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: The prince pleaded several times; unable to refuse, the court appointed Chen Pacifying West Chief Clerk and Administrator of Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The prince pleaded repeatedly; at last the court appointed Chen chief clerk of Pacifying West and Administrator of Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 在蜀廉恪為政，益部懷之。

translations.literal: In Shu he governed with integrity and frugality; the Yi region cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu he governed with integrity and frugality, and the region held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 憕弟忱。

translations.literal: Chen's younger brother Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's younger brother was Xin.

sentences.zh: 忱字文若，年數歲，父世隆及母閻氏並疾，忱不解帶經年，及居喪以毀聞。

translations.literal: Chen Xin, style name Wenruo, at several years of age when father Shilong and mother Lady Yan were both ill, did not unfasten his belt for a year; in mourning he was known for devastating grief.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xin, styled Wenruo, was only a few years old when both his father Shilong and mother Lady Yan fell ill; he kept his belt tied for a year, and in mourning he was famed for devastating grief.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為西中郎主簿。

translations.literal: In Qi he served as Chief Clerk of the Western Center Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as chief clerk of the Western Center Army.

sentences.zh: 東昏遣巴西太守劉山陽由荊州襲梁武帝於雍州，西中郎長史蕭穎胄計未定，召忱及其所親席闡文等夜入議之。

translations.literal: Donghun sent Administrator of Baxi Liu Shanyang from Jingzhou to strike Liang Emperor Wu in Yongzhou; Western Center Army Chief Clerk Xiao Yinggou's plan was undecided, and he summoned Chen Xin and his intimate Xi Kanwen and others to enter at night to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun sent Liu Shanyang, Administrator of Baxi, from Jing Province to attack the future Emperor Wu in Yong Province; Chief Clerk Xiao Yinggou had not decided on a course and summoned Chen Xin, Xi Kanwen, and others for a night council.

sentences.zh: 忱及闡文並勸同武帝，穎胄從之。

translations.literal: Chen Xin and Kanwen both urged joining Emperor Wu, and Yinggou followed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xin and Kanwen both urged alliance with the future emperor, and Yinggou agreed.

sentences.zh: 以忱為甯朔將軍，累遷侍中。

translations.literal: Chen Xin was made General Who Pacifies the North and was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xin was made General Who Pacifies the North and rose to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 郢州平，穎胄議遷都夏口，忱以巴峽未賓，不宜輕舍根本，搖動人心，不從。

translations.literal: When Yingzhou was pacified, Yinggou proposed moving the capital to Xiakou; Chen Xin held that Ba Gorge was not yet submitted, and one should not lightly abandon the root and shake men's hearts—this was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: After Ying Province was secured, Yinggou proposed moving the capital to Xiakou; Chen Xin argued that Ba and the gorges were not yet pacified and that abandoning the base would unsettle men's hearts; his counsel prevailed.

sentences.zh: 俄而巴東兵至峽口，遷都之議乃息。

translations.literal: Soon Ba East troops reached the gorge mouth, and the proposal to move the capital ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Eastern Ba forces reached the gorge, and the move was dropped.

sentences.zh: 論者以為見機。

translations.literal: Commentators considered this perceiving the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators praised his foresight.

sentences.zh: 及梁受命，封州陵伯。

translations.literal: When Liang received the Mandate, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder took the throne, Chen Xin was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling.

sentences.zh: 曆五兵尚書，秘書監，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Director of the Five Armies, Director of the Secretariat, and Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of the Five Armies, Director of the Secretariat, and Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 改授給事中、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Supernumerary Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Supernumerary Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 疾篤不拜。

translations.literal: He was gravely ill and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was too ill to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously titled Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous title Reverent.

sentences.zh: 忱兄弟十五人，多少亡，唯第二兄惔、第三兄惲、第四兄憕及忱三兩年間四人疊為侍中，復居方伯，當世罕比。

translations.literal: Chen had fifteen brothers; many had already died. Only his second elder brother Tan, third elder brother Yun, fourth elder brother Cheng, and Chen himself—in the space of two or three years the four of them successively served as Attendants-in-Ordinary and again held governorships of provinces—such a thing was rarely matched in their day.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had fifteen brothers, most of whom had already died. Only his second brother Tan, third brother Yun, fourth brother Cheng, and Chen himself—in the span of two or three years all four successively held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary and provincial governorships, a distinction rarely equaled in their generation.

sentences.zh: 子範嗣。

translations.literal: His son Fan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan succeeded to his position.

sentences.zh: 慶遠字文和，元景弟子也。

translations.literal: Qingyuan, styled Wenhe, was Yuanjing's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qingyuan, styled Wenhe, was the nephew of Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 父叔珍，義陽內史。

translations.literal: His father Shuzhen was Interior Administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuzhen served as Interior Administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 慶遠仕齊為魏興太守，郡遭暴水，人欲移於杞城。

translations.literal: Qingyuan served Qi as Administrator of Weixing; the commandery suffered a sudden flood, and the people wished to relocate to Qicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan served under the Qi as Administrator of Weixing. When the commandery was struck by a sudden flood, the people wanted to move to Qicheng.

sentences.zh: 慶遠曰：「吾聞江河長不過三日，命築土而已。

translations.literal: Qingyuan said: "I have heard that rivers in flood last no more than three days. Order only that earthworks be built."
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan said, "I have heard that river floods never last more than three days. Simply order earthworks to be built."

sentences.zh: 」俄而水退，百姓服之。

translations.literal: Before long the waters receded, and the common people were impressed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the floodwaters receded, and the people were won over.

sentences.zh: 後為襄陽令，梁武帝之臨雍州，問京兆人杜惲求州綱紀，惲言慶遠。

translations.literal: Later he served as Magistrate of Xiangyang. When Emperor Wu of Liang took up his post at Yong Province, he asked Du Yun of Jingzhao to recommend someone to serve as the province's chief administrator; Yun named Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Magistrate of Xiangyang. When Emperor Wu of Liang assumed his post in Yong Province, he asked Du Yun of Jingzhao to recommend a chief administrator for the province, and Yun named Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 武帝曰：「文和吾已知之，所問未知者耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Wenhe I already know; it is someone unknown to me that I am asking about."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I already know Wenhe—it is someone I do not yet know that I am asking about."

sentences.zh: 」因辟為別駕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was summoned as Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, Qingyuan was summoned to serve as Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 慶遠謂所親曰：「天下方亂，定霸者其吾君乎。

translations.literal: Qingyuan said to those close to him: "The realm is in turmoil; is it not our lord who will establish supremacy?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan said to his intimates, "The realm is in turmoil—is it not our lord who will win the hegemony?"

sentences.zh: 」因盡誠協贊。

translations.literal: Accordingly he devoted himself wholeheartedly to supporting him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore devoted himself wholeheartedly to supporting him.

sentences.zh: 及起兵，慶遠常居帷幄為謀主，從軍東下，身先士卒。

translations.literal: When troops were raised, Qingyuan constantly stayed within the command tent as chief strategist; marching east with the army, he led from the front.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was raised, Qingyuan regularly remained in the command tent as chief strategist. Marching east with the forces, he always led from the front.

sentences.zh: 武帝行營，見慶遠頓舍嚴整，每歎曰：「人人若是，吾又何憂。

translations.literal: On inspection tours of the camp, the Emperor saw Qingyuan's encampments rigorously ordered and would sigh each time: "If every man were like this, what would I have to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: On his rounds through the camp, Emperor Wu saw that Qingyuan's encampments were rigorously ordered and would sigh each time, "If every man were like this, what would I have to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 」建康城平，為侍中，帶淮陵齊昌二郡太守。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was taken, he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Administrator of the two commanderies of Huailing and Qichang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang was taken, he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently served as Administrator of the commanderies of Huailing and Qichang.

sentences.zh: 城內嘗夜火，眾並驚懼。

translations.literal: Once a fire broke out in the city at night, and everyone was alarmed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Once a fire broke out in the city at night, and the whole populace was alarmed and afraid.

sentences.zh: 武帝時居宮中，悉斂諸門鑰，問柳侍中何在。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then inside the palace; he gathered all the gate keys and asked where Attendant Liu was.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then inside the palace. He gathered all the gate keys and asked where Attendant Liu was.

sentences.zh: 慶遠至，悉付之，其見任如此。

translations.literal: When Qingyuan arrived, the Emperor handed them all over to him—such was the degree of trust placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingyuan arrived, the Emperor entrusted them all to him—such was the trust he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 霸府建，為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When the overlord's headquarters was established, he was made Aide-de-Camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the overlord's headquarters was established, he was appointed Aide-de-Camp.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封重安侯，位散騎常侍，改封雲杜侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chong'an and appointed Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry; his title was later changed to Marquis of Yundu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, Qingyuan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chong'an and appointed Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry; his title was later changed to Marquis of Yundu.

sentences.zh: 出為雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Inspector of Yong Province with augmented authority as Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Yong Province with the added title of Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 帝餞於新亭，謂曰：「卿衣錦還鄉，朕無西顧憂矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw him off at Xinting and said: "You return to your homeland in glory; I need no longer worry about the west."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw him off at Xinting and said, "You return home in glory—I need no longer worry about the west."

sentences.zh: 」始武帝為雍州，慶遠為別駕，謂曰：「昔羊公語劉弘，卿後當居吾處。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Emperor Wu held Yong Province and Qingyuan was his Vice Director, he told him: "In the past Yang Hu said to Liu Hong, 'You will afterward occupy my place.'"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Wu held Yong Province and Qingyuan served as his Vice Director, he had told him, "In the past Yang Hu said to Liu Hong, 'You will afterward occupy my place.'"

sentences.zh: 今相觀亦復如是。

translations.literal: Now as I look upon you, it is again just so.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as I look at you, it is again just so.

sentences.zh: 」曾未十年，而慶遠督府，談者以為逾于魏詠之。

translations.literal: In less than ten years, Qingyuan was governing the province, and commentators held that he surpassed Wei Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten years Qingyuan was governing the province, and commentators held that he surpassed Wei Yongzhi.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中、領軍將軍，給扶。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Leads the Army, and was granted a staff for support.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Leads the Army, and was granted a walking staff.

sentences.zh: 出為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out again as Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent out as Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 慶遠重為本州，頗厲清節，士庶懷之。

translations.literal: Serving his home province a second time, Qingyuan greatly enforced integrity; officials and commoners alike cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Serving his home province a second time, Qingyuan strongly upheld integrity, and officials and commoners alike held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰忠惠侯。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously he was given the title of Grand Warden with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, and was posthumously enfeoffed as the Reverent and Gracious Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office. Posthumously he was granted the title of Grand Warden with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies and received the posthumous title Reverent and Gracious Marquis.

sentences.zh: 喪還都，武帝親出臨之。

translations.literal: When the funeral procession returned to the capital, the Emperor personally went out to attend it.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession returned to the capital, Emperor Wu personally went out to attend it.

sentences.zh: 初，慶遠從父兄世隆嘗謂慶遠曰：「吾昔夢太尉以褥席見賜，吾遂亞台司。

translations.literal: At the outset, Qingyuan's older first cousin Shilong once said to Qingyuan: "In the past I dreamed that the Grand Commandant bestowed mattress and mat on me, and I indeed came to rank second among the Three Excellencies."
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Qingyuan's older first cousin Shilong once said to him, "In the past I dreamed that the Grand Commandant bestowed mattress and mat on me, and I indeed came to rank second among the Three Excellencies."

sentences.zh: 適又夢以吾褥席與汝，汝必光我門族。

translations.literal: Just now I have again dreamed of giving you my mattress and mat—you will surely bring glory to our clan.
translations.idiomatic: Just now I have again dreamed of giving you my mattress and mat—you will surely bring glory to our clan.

sentences.zh: 」至是慶遠亦繼世隆焉。

translations.literal: By this point Qingyuan too had succeeded Shilong in such station.
translations.idiomatic: By this time Qingyuan too had succeeded Shilong in such station.

sentences.zh: 子津字元舉，雖乏風華，性甚強直。

translations.literal: His son Jin, styled Yuanju, though lacking literary grace, was by nature very forceful and upright.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Jin, styled Yuanju, though lacking literary polish, was by nature very forceful and upright.

sentences.zh: 人或勸之聚書，津曰：「吾常請道士上章驅鬼，安用此鬼名邪。

translations.literal: When someone urged him to amass books, Jin said: "I often ask Daoist priests to submit memorials to drive away ghosts—what use have I for these ghost-names?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged him to amass books, Jin said, "I often ask Daoist priests to submit memorials to drive away ghosts—what use have I for these ghost-names?"

sentences.zh: 」曆散騎常侍，太子詹事，襲封雲杜侯。

translations.literal: He served successively as Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and inherited the marquisate of Yundu.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and inherited the marquisate of Yundu.

sentences.zh: 侯景圍城既急，帝召津問策。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing's siege of the city had grown critical, the Emperor summoned Jin to ask his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing's siege of the city had grown critical, the Emperor summoned Jin to ask his counsel.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下有邵陵，臣有仲禮，不忠不孝，賊何由可平。

translations.literal: He answered: "Your Majesty has Prince Shaoling, and I have Zhongli—between disloyalty and unfilial conduct, how can the rebels ever be crushed?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty has Prince Lun of Shaoling, and I have Zhongli—with disloyalty on one side and unfilial conduct on the other, how can the rebels ever be crushed?"

sentences.zh: 」太清三年，城陷，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing the city fell, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing the city fell, and he died.

sentences.zh: 子仲禮，勇力兼人，少有膽氣，身長八尺，眉目疏朗。

translations.literal: His son Zhongli combined the strength of several men; from youth he had daring spirit; he stood eight feet tall, with broad, clear features.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Zhongli possessed the strength of several men. From youth he had daring spirit; he stood eight feet tall, with broad, clear features.

sentences.zh: 初，簡文帝為雍州刺史，津為長史。

translations.literal: At the outset, when Emperor Jianwen was Inspector of Yong Province, Jin served as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, when Emperor Jianwen was Inspector of Yong Province, Jin served as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 及簡文入居儲宮，津亦得侍從。

translations.literal: When Jianwen entered the Eastern Palace as heir, Jin likewise obtained a place in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen entered the Eastern Palace as heir apparent, Jin likewise obtained a place in attendance.

sentences.zh: 仲禮留在襄陽，馬仗軍人悉付之。

translations.literal: Zhongli remained at Xiangyang, and all horses, weapons, and troops were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli remained at Xiangyang, and all horses, weapons, and troops were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 撫循故舊，甚得眾和。

translations.literal: He cared for old associates and won the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for old associates and won the hearts of the troops.

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎，稍遷電威將軍，陽泉縣侯。

translations.literal: He began his career as an Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and was gradually promoted to General of Lightning Awe and Marquis of Yangquan County.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as an Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and was gradually promoted to General of Lightning Awe and Marquis of Yangquan County.

sentences.zh: 中大通中，西魏將賀拔勝來逼樊、鄧，仲禮出擊破之。

translations.literal: In the Zhongdatong era, the Western Wei general Helaba Sheng pressed upon Fan and Deng; Zhongli went out and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhongdatong era, the Western Wei general Helaba Sheng pressed upon Fan and Deng; Zhongli went out and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 除黃門郎，稍遷司州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and gradually promoted to Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and gradually promoted to Inspector of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 武帝思見其面，使畫工圖之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu longed to see his face and had a painter depict him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu longed to see his face in person and had a painter depict him.

sentences.zh: 初，侯景潛圖反噬，仲禮先知之，屢啟求以精兵三萬討景，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: At the outset, Hou Jing secretly plotted revolt; Zhongli foresaw it first and repeatedly submitted memorials asking leave to take thirty thousand picked troops to attack Jing—the court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Hou Jing secretly plotted rebellion. Zhongli foresaw it first and repeatedly submitted memorials asking to take thirty thousand picked troops to attack him, but the court would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 及景濟江，朝野便望其至。

translations.literal: When Jing crossed the Yangtze, court and countryside alike looked eagerly for his arrival.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze, court and countryside alike looked eagerly for Zhongli's arrival.

sentences.zh: 兼蓄雍、司精卒，與諸蕃赴援，見推總督。

translations.literal: Gathering elite troops from Yong and Si provinces, he marched with the various princes to the rescue and was chosen as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering elite troops from Yong and Si provinces, he marched with the various princes to the rescue and was chosen as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 景素聞其名，甚憚之。

translations.literal: Jing had long heard his name and greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing had long heard his name and greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 仲禮亦自謂當世英雄，諸將莫己若也。

translations.literal: Zhongli likewise considered himself the hero of the age, and no general was his equal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli likewise considered himself the hero of the age, and believed no general was his equal.

sentences.zh: 韋粲見攻，仲禮方食，投箸被練馳之，騎能屬者七十。

translations.literal: When Wei Can came under attack, Zhongli was at his meal; he cast down his chopsticks, threw on plain armor, and spurred there—seventy riders could keep pace with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Can came under attack, Zhongli was at his meal. He cast down his chopsticks, threw on plain armor, and spurred there—only seventy riders could keep pace with him.

sentences.zh: 比至，粲已敗，仲禮因與景戰於青塘，大敗之。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Can had already been defeated; Zhongli thereupon joined battle with Jing at Qingtang and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, Can had already been defeated. Zhongli thereupon joined battle with Hou Jing at Qingtang and routed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 景與仲禮交戰，各不相知。

translations.literal: Jing and Zhongli fought each other without recognizing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing and Zhongli fought each other without recognizing one another.

sentences.zh: 仲禮矟將及景，而賊將支伯仁自後斫仲禮，再斫仲禮中肩。

translations.literal: Zhongli's spear was about to reach Jing when the rebel general Zhi Boren struck from behind, twice cutting Zhongli in the shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli's spear was about to reach Hou Jing when the rebel general Zhi Boren struck from behind, twice cutting Zhongli in the shoulder.

sentences.zh: 馬陷於淖，賊聚矟刺之，騎將郭山石救之以免。

translations.literal: His horse sank in the mud; the rebels massed spears to stab him, and the cavalry commander Guo Shanshi rescued him so he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His horse sank in the mud; the rebels massed spears to stab him, and the cavalry commander Guo Shanshi rescued him so that he escaped.

sentences.zh: 自此壯氣外衰，不復言戰。

translations.literal: From this point his bold spirit waned outwardly, and he spoke of battle no more.
translations.idiomatic: From this point his bold spirit waned outwardly, and he spoke of battle no more.

sentences.zh: 神情傲佷，淩蔑將帥。

translations.literal: His bearing was proud and obstinate; he looked down on commanders and generals.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was proud and obstinate, and he looked down on commanders and generals.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸亦鞭策軍門，每日必至，累刻移時，仲禮亦弗見也。

translations.literal: Prince Lun of Shaoling also came daily to whip his horse at the camp gate and waited for hours on end, yet Zhongli would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Shaoling also came daily to the camp gate, whipping his horse and waiting for hours on end, yet Zhongli would not see him.

sentences.zh: 綸既忿歎，怨隙遂成。

translations.literal: Lun, filled with resentment and lament, and enmity thereupon took form.
translations.idiomatic: Filled with resentment and lament, Lun and Zhongli thereupon became enemies.

sentences.zh: 而仲禮常置酒高會，日作優倡，毒掠百姓，污辱妃主。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Zhongli constantly held grand banquets and feasts, daily staging entertainers; he tyrannized and plundered the common people and defiled imperial consorts and princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhongli constantly held grand banquets and feasts, daily staging entertainers; he tyrannized and plundered the common people and defiled imperial consorts and princesses.

sentences.zh: 父津登城謂曰：「汝君父在難，不能盡心竭力，百代之後，謂汝為何。

translations.literal: His father Jin mounted the wall and said to him: "Your sovereign and father are in peril, yet you cannot devote heart and strength—what will posterity call you a hundred generations hence?"
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin mounted the city wall and said to him, "Your sovereign and father are in peril, yet you cannot devote heart and strength—what will posterity call you a hundred generations hence?"

sentences.zh: 」仲禮聞之，言笑自若。

translations.literal: Zhongli heard this and continued talking and laughing as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli heard this and continued talking and laughing as before.

sentences.zh: 晚又與臨城公大連不協。

translations.literal: Later he also fell out with the Duke of Lincheng, Dalian.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also fell out with the Duke of Lincheng, Dalian.

sentences.zh: 景嘗登朱雀樓與之語，遺以金環。

translations.literal: Jing once mounted the Vermilion Bird Tower to speak with him and presented him with a gold ring.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing once mounted the Vermilion Bird Tower to speak with him and presented him with a gold ring.

sentences.zh: 是後閉營不戰，眾軍日固請，皆悉拒焉。

translations.literal: After this he kept his camp shut and would not fight; the allied armies daily pressed him insistently, but he refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: After this he kept his camp shut and would not fight. The allied armies pressed him daily to battle, but he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 南安侯駿謂曰：「城急如此，都督不復處分，如脫不守，何面以見天下義士。

translations.literal: Marquis Jun of Nan'an said to him: "The city is in such desperate straits, yet the commander-in-chief no longer issues orders. If it should fall after all, with what face will you meet the men of righteousness under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jun of Nan'an said to him, "The city is in such desperate straits, yet the commander-in-chief no longer issues orders. If it should fall after all, with what face will you meet the men of righteousness under Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」仲禮無以應之。

translations.literal: Zhongli had nothing to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli had nothing to answer.

sentences.zh: 及台城陷，侯景矯詔使石城公大款以白虎幡解諸軍。

translations.literal: When Taicheng fell, Hou Jing forged an edict sending the Duke of Shicheng, Dakuan, to dismiss the armies with a White Tiger banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Taicheng fell, Hou Jing forged an edict sending the Duke of Shicheng, Dakuan, to dismiss the armies with a White Tiger banner.

sentences.zh: 仲禮召諸將軍會議，邵陵王以下畢集。

translations.literal: Zhongli summoned the generals to council; from Prince Shaoling downward all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli summoned the generals to council; from Prince Lun of Shaoling downward all assembled.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「今日之命，委之將軍。

translations.literal: The prince said: "Today's decision rests with the general."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Today's decision rests with the general."

sentences.zh: 」仲禮熟視不對。

translations.literal: Zhongli stared at him fixedly and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli stared at him fixedly and did not reply.

sentences.zh: 裴之高、王僧辯曰：「將軍擁眾百萬，致宮闕淪沒，正當悉力決戰，何所多言。

translations.literal: Pei Zhigao and Wang Sengbian said: "The general commands a force of a million, yet the palace has fallen to ruin—you should right now commit every strength to decisive battle; what need for so much talk?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhigao and Wang Sengbian said, "The general commands a force of a million, yet the palace has fallen to ruin—you should right now commit every strength to decisive battle. What need for so much talk?"

sentences.zh: 」仲禮竟無一言，諸軍乃隨方各散。

translations.literal: Zhongli ultimately said not a word, and the armies thereupon dispersed each to its own quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli ultimately said not a word, and the armies thereupon dispersed each to its own quarter.

sentences.zh: 時湘東王繹遣王琳送米二十萬石以饋軍，至姑孰聞台城陷，乃沈米于江而退。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Yi of Xiangdong sent Wang Lin with two hundred thousand shi of rice to supply the army; reaching Gudu he heard that Taicheng had fallen, whereupon he sank the rice in the river and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Yi of Xiangdong sent Wang Lin with two hundred thousand shi of rice to supply the army. Reaching Gudu, he heard that Taicheng had fallen, whereupon he sank the rice in the river and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 仲禮及弟敬禮、羊鴉仁、王僧辯、趙伯超並開營降賊。

translations.literal: Zhongli, together with his younger brother Jingli, Yang Yaren, Wang Sengbian, and Zhao Bochao, all opened their camps and submitted to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli, together with his younger brother Liu Jingli, Yang Yaren, Wang Sengbian, and Zhao Bochao, all opened their camps and submitted to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時城雖淪陷，援軍甚眾，軍士咸欲盡力，及聞降，莫不歎憤。

translations.literal: Although the city had fallen, the relief armies were still numerous and the soldiers all wished to fight to the utmost; when they heard of the surrender, none failed to sigh in grief and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Although the city had fallen, the relief armies were still numerous and the soldiers all wished to fight to the utmost. When they heard of the surrender, none failed to sigh in grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 論者以為梁禍始于朱異，成于仲禮。

translations.literal: Commentators held that Liang's calamity began with Zhu Yi and was brought to completion by Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that Liang's calamity began with Zhu Yi and was brought to completion by Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 仲禮等入城，並先拜景而後見帝，帝不與言。

translations.literal: When Zhongli and the others entered the city, they all bowed first to Jing and only afterward saw the Emperor; the Emperor would not speak to them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongli and the others entered the city, they all bowed first to Hou Jing and only afterward saw the Emperor; the Emperor would not speak to them.

sentences.zh: 既而景留柳敬禮、羊鴉仁，而遣仲禮、僧辯西上，各復本位。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Jing detained Liu Jingli and Yang Yaren, but sent Zhongli and Sengbian westward to return each to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Hou Jing detained Liu Jingli and Yang Yaren, but sent Zhongli and Sengbian westward to return each to his former post.

sentences.zh: 餞于後渚，景執仲禮手曰：「天下之事在將軍耳。

translations.literal: At a farewell at Houzhu, Jing took Zhongli's hand and said: "The affairs of the realm rest upon the general."
translations.idiomatic: At a farewell at Houzhu, Hou Jing took Zhongli's hand and said, "The affairs of the realm rest upon the general."

sentences.zh: 郢州、巴西並以相付。」

translations.literal: Ying Province and Basi are both entrusted to you."
translations.idiomatic: Ying Province and Basi are both entrusted to you."

sentences.zh: 及至江陵，會岳陽王察南寇，湘東王以仲禮為雍州刺史，襲襄陽。

translations.literal: When they reached Jiangling, Prince Cha of Yueyang was raiding southward; Prince Yi of Xiangdong appointed Zhongli Inspector of Yong Province to assault Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Jiangling, Prince Cha of Yueyang was raiding southward. Prince Yi of Xiangdong appointed Zhongli Inspector of Yong Province to assault Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 仲禮方觀成敗，未發。

translations.literal: Zhongli was still watching how success and failure would fall and had not yet set out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli was still watching how success and failure would fall and had not yet set out.

sentences.zh: 及南陽圍急，杜岸請救，仲禮乃以別將夏侯強為司州刺史，守義陽，自帥眾如安陸，使司馬康昭如竟陵討孫暠。

translations.literal: When the siege of Nanyang grew urgent, Du An requested aid. Zhongli thereupon made the subordinate general Xia Houqiang Inspector of Si Province to hold Yiyang; he himself led troops toward Anlu and sent Chief Clerk Kang Zhao to Jingling to subdue Sun Gao.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege of Nanyang grew urgent, Du An requested aid. Zhongli thereupon made the subordinate general Xia Houqiang Inspector of Si Province to hold Yiyang; he himself led troops toward Anlu and sent Chief Clerk Kang Zhao to Jingling to subdue Sun Gao.

sentences.zh: 暠執魏戍人以降。

translations.literal: Gao captured Wei garrison troops and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gao captured Wei garrison troops and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 仲禮命其將王叔孫為竟陵太守，副軍馬岫為安陸太守。

translations.literal: Zhongli appointed his general Wang Shusun Administrator of Jingling and his lieutenant Ma Xiu Administrator of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli appointed his general Wang Shusun Administrator of Jingling and his lieutenant Ma Xiu Administrator of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 置孥于安陸，而以輕兵師於漴頭，將侵襄陽。

translations.literal: He stationed his family at Anlu and led light troops to camp at Chongtou, intending to invade Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed his family at Anlu and led light troops to camp at Chongtou, intending to invade Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 岳陽王察告急于魏，魏遣大將楊忠援之。

translations.literal: Prince Cha of Yueyang urgently appealed to Wei; Wei sent the great general Yang Zhong to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cha of Yueyang urgently appealed to Wei, and Wei sent the great general Yang Zhong to aid him.

sentences.zh: 仲禮與戰於漴頭，大敗，並弟子禮沒于魏。

translations.literal: Zhongli fought at Chongtou and suffered a crushing defeat; together with his younger cousin Li he was captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli fought at Chongtou and suffered a crushing defeat; together with his younger cousin Li he was captured by Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏相安定公待仲禮以客禮。

translations.literal: The Wei Chancellor, the Duke of Anding, treated Zhongli with the courtesy due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Chancellor, the Duke of Anding, treated Zhongli with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 西魏於是盡得漢東。

translations.literal: The Western Wei thereby gained the whole of Handong.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei thereby gained the whole of the eastern Han River region.

sentences.zh: 仲禮弟敬禮，少以勇烈聞。

translations.literal: Zhongli's younger brother Jingli was known from youth for courage and fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli's younger brother Liu Jingli was known from youth for courage and fierceness.

sentences.zh: 粗暴無行檢，恒略賣人，為百姓所苦，故襄陽有柳四郎歌。

translations.literal: Violent and coarse, without moral restraint, he constantly abducted and sold people; the common people suffered under him, and so Xiangyang had the "Song of the Fourth Son Liu."
translations.idiomatic: Violent and coarse, without moral restraint, he constantly abducted and sold people. The common people suffered under him, and so Xiangyang had the "Song of the Fourth Son Liu."

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎，稍遷扶風太守。

translations.literal: He began his career as an Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and was gradually promoted to Administrator of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as an Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and was gradually promoted to Administrator of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 侯景度江，敬禮率馬步三千赴援。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze, Jingli led three thousand cavalry and infantry to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze, Liu Jingli led three thousand cavalry and infantry to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 至都，與景頻戰，甚著威名。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital, he fought Jing repeatedly and won a great reputation for martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the capital, he fought Hou Jing repeatedly and won a great reputation for martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，與兄仲禮俱見景，景遣仲禮經略上流，留敬禮質，以為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, he and his elder brother Zhongli both had audience with Hou Jing; Jing sent Zhongli to manage the upper reaches, kept Jingli as hostage, and appointed him General of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, he and his brother Zhongli were brought before Hou Jing; Jing sent Zhongli to secure the upper Yangtze, kept Jingli as a hostage, and made him General of the Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 景餞仲禮於後渚。

translations.literal: Jing gave Zhongli a farewell feast at Rear Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing gave Zhongli a farewell feast at Rear Ford.

sentences.zh: 敬禮謂仲禮曰：「景今來會，敬禮抱之，兄便可殺，雖死無恨。

translations.literal: Jingli said to Zhongli: "When Jing comes to the meeting today, I will embrace him—then you can kill him at once; though I die, I shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Jingli told Zhongli: "When Jing comes to the feast, I will seize him in my arms—you can strike then and kill him. If I die in the attempt, I shall not regret it."

sentences.zh: 」仲禮壯其言，許之。

translations.literal: Zhongli admired his words and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli admired his courage and agreed.

sentences.zh: 及酒數行，敬禮目仲禮，仲禮見備衛嚴，不敢動，遂不果。

translations.literal: After several rounds of wine, Jingli signaled Zhongli with his eyes; Zhongli saw the guards were strict and dared not move—the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After several rounds of wine Jingli signaled his brother, but Zhongli saw how heavily Jing was guarded and dared not act; the plot came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 會景征晉熙，敬禮與南康王會理謀襲其城，克期將發，建安侯蕭賁告之，遂遇害。

translations.literal: When Jing campaigned against Jinxi, Jingli with Prince Huili of Nankang plotted to storm his city; the day was set and they were about to move when Marquis Jian'an Xiao Ben informed on them, and Jingli was killed.
translations.idiomatic: While Hou Jing was campaigning against Jinxi, Jingli and Prince Huili of Nankang plotted to seize his city; on the eve of action Marquis Jian'an Xiao Ben betrayed them, and Jingli was put to death.

sentences.zh: 臨死曰：「我兄老婢也，國敗家亡，實餘之責，今日就死，豈非天乎。」

translations.literal: Facing death he said: "My brother is an old woman; the state is defeated and the house destroyed—the blame is truly mine. To die today—is this not Heaven's will?"
translations.idiomatic: At the end he said: "My brother is a timid old woman; the state is ruined and our house destroyed, and the fault is truly mine. To die today—can this be anything but Heaven's decree?"

sentences.zh: 論曰：柳元景行己所資，豈徒武毅；

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the resources of Liu Yuanjing's conduct of himself, was it only martial resolution?
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Liu Yuanjing's conduct drew on more than martial resolution alone;

sentences.zh: 當朝任職，實兼雅道。

translations.literal: In holding office at court, he truly combined refined principle.
translations.idiomatic: in high office he embodied cultivated principle as well.

sentences.zh: 卒至覆族，遭逢亦有命乎。

translations.literal: Yet in the end his clan was overthrown—perhaps one's encounters also lie in fate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his clan was destroyed in the end—perhaps such a fate was ordained.

sentences.zh: 世隆文武器業，殆人望也，諸子門素所傳，俱雲克構。

translations.literal: Shilong's civil and military accomplishments were nearly the hope of men; the sons of the house had long been said to transmit this, and all declared they would build on it.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's civil and military gifts made him the hope of his age; the sons of the house were all said to inherit his promise and build on his legacy.

sentences.zh: 仲禮始終之際，其不副也何哉？

translations.literal: At the beginning and end, how did Zhongli fail to measure up?
translations.idiomatic: How did Zhongli, from first to last, fall so far short?

sentences.zh: 豈應天方喪梁，不然，何斯人而有斯跡也。

translations.literal: Was it because Heaven was just then bringing Liang to ruin? Otherwise, how could such a man leave such a record?
translations.idiomatic: Was it because Heaven had already doomed Liang? Otherwise, how could a man of such promise leave such a record of shame?
